Add your VPN provider's or your home router's WireGuard file (an administrator's password), then connect and disconnect there or from the taskbar's network pop-up, which shows its state. While it is on, every app's traffic and its name lookups go through it, the local network is still reached directly, and nothing goes round it by IPv6. Its key is kept where only the system reads it. The same on Native, Chromium and Lite.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: who may turn each VPN on and off, an administrator's choice: Everyone (the default), Administrators only, or Always on (it comes back at every start and nobody can turn it off). Accounts with parental controls cannot turn a VPN off, and turning off a VPN another account turned on says so first ("Ann's VPN is on for everyone on this computer").

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: a VPN's kill switch (an administrator's, off at first): while a VPN with it is meant to be on and its tunnel is down, nothing goes out but the VPN's own server, until it is back or turned off.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Settings › Network › VPN says that Oracle's Tor windows then run inside the VPN.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: OpenVPN VPNs: add a provider's .ovpn file the same way (with its username and password when it asks for them). Rudolf OS runs OpenVPN only while that VPN is on; files that would run scripts or plugins are refused.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: on the native desktop the taskbar's pinned apps and workspace buttons kept their light grey edge in dark mode, where Chromium mode draws a dim one, and a pinned app had no line under it while its window was open (grey, or the accent colour while that window is the active one). Both now look as in Chromium mode, on every monitor's taskbar. The "Several monitors" check compares both looks, light and dark, whatever the hour it runs at.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Kernel: the SMB client for network shares (Windows computers and NAS boxes, 1.6.2 Part 35) is built in as a signed module, loaded only when a share is opened. It speaks SMB 3 (and SMB 2.1 when asked for a share), never the old SMB 1 or 2.0, and Rudolf OS serves no share.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New (for File Explorer's network shares, Part 35): Rudolf OS can open a shared folder of a Windows computer or a NAS box for the account signed in. Its files are that account's alone (other accounts cannot see it), the server is asked to encrypt where it can, the password is kept in the account's keyring only if asked, and every share closes at sign-out. A wrong password, a missing share or a server that speaks only the old SMB 1 is said plainly.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Network in File Explorer. It lists the Windows computers and NAS boxes found on your home network (with the firewall on) and opens their shared folders as folders of your own: browse, open, copy to and from, drag onto the desktop. You can also type a share's address (\\server\share or smb://server/share). Your recent shares are listed and reconnect only when you open them, never at start-up, so a server that is off never slows the start. Disconnect closes a share. The same on Native, Chromium and Lite.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: scanners (step 1 of 4: driverless scanning, without the Scan app yet). Rudolf OS finds the scanners and printer-scanners on the home network that speak eSCL (AirScan) or WSD, as most made since about 2015 do, with the firewall on, and USB ones that speak eSCL through IPP over USB; it scans with sane-airscan (pages in colour, grey or black and white, an area, the resolution, the document feeder's pages) and saves PDF, PNG or JPEG. Scanning runs as the account's own user. 495 KB more on the disk; nothing runs until a scan.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Scan, an app of Rudolf's own for those scanners (step 2 of 4), in the Start menu, in File Explorer (Scan into this folder), in the Print dialog and in Settings › Devices: the scanners found, a preview, the area drawn on it or a paper size, colour, grey or black and white, the resolution, the glass or the document feeder; pages added one scan after another, put in order or taken out, then saved as one PDF, or each page as PNG or JPEG, in Documents or where you choose. A paper jam, the cover open, an empty feeder, a busy scanner or none found are said plainly. Scanning runs as your account's own user, which also writes the file. The same on Native, Chromium and Lite.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: older USB scanners (step 3 of 4): eight of SANE's own drivers for scanners that need one, chosen by what is common: Canon PIXMA and CanoScan (pixma, genesys, plustek, canon_lide70), Epson (epson2, epsonds), Samsung, Xerox and Dell all-in-ones (xerox_mfp) and Fujitsu document scanners (fujitsu). They work only over USB, and the scanner is given to your account's own user only while it scans. 2.4 MB more on the disk.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Linux apps such as Simple Scan use the network scanners Rudolf OS found (step 4 of 4): after Scan has looked for scanners, their addresses are given read-only to the Debian sandbox's own scanning settings. USB scanners stay with Rudolf's Scan app: Linux apps get no USB devices.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: with the taskbar at the left or the right, Quick settings, the notifications and the calendar open beside their buttons (they opened in the screen's bottom-right corner, over a taskbar at the right); a right-click menu no longer lies over the taskbar; and the desktop's icons move at once when the taskbar grows instead of sitting under it. The same on Native.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Kernel: the system's images can be packed with zstd (squashfs reads zstd as well as xz, on x86-64 and ARM64). The images themselves are unchanged in this version; a later one moves them to zstd once every updated computer can read them.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Updates: an update whose system images its own kernel could not read is refused with a message saying so (when it is checked, and again once downloaded), as are the recovery system and Make a stick; nothing on the computer is changed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Updates: when an update packs the system's images in a new way (as the move to zstd does), Settings › Update says before downloading that they come whole this once, and how much ("Download (about 530 MB)"), on every connection; later updates download only the changes again. The download no longer tries the changes first for such an image.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Desert Camp, a third moving background (Display Properties › Dynamic Backgrounds): an open desert with clusters of tents round their campfires. At sunrise the sun comes up as a shimmering mirage on the horizon and the campfires smoke; at night the tents glow from inside, the fires flicker, the stars twinkle under a nebula and shooting stars streak by. The same on Native, Chromium and Lite.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: Nintendo 64 and Dreamcast games in Emu never started. Starting one stopped Rudolf OS's system service (it restarts by itself) before the emulator opened. Now Rosalie's Mupen GUI and Flycast open with the game, full screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: Nintendo 64 games had no controls. Rosalie's Mupen GUI connects no controller until its settings have been saved once, and Emu opens it without its menus. Player 1 is now set up the first time a game starts: the first controller, or the keyboard (the arrow keys are the stick, X is A, C is B, Z is Z, Return is Start). A setup you saved in its settings (Ctrl+I) is kept.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: Nintendo 64 games end with F12, and the emulator then closes. Emu's note said Esc, which did nothing there, and ending the game left an empty window.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: When Emu closed a Nintendo 64 or Dreamcast game to start another, the emulator kept running. The same was true of Sober (Roblox) when Rudolf OS closed it. They now end completely.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: the plan (docs/plan-1.6.2.md Parts 33 to 35): a VPN for the whole computer (WireGuard, then OpenVPN; an administrator adds them, everyone may turn them on and off unless told otherwise; an optional kill switch), scanners (driverless first, with a Scan app) and network shares (Windows and NAS shares in File Explorer).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: Bring your files now opens an old Windows disk's BitLocker for real. It was checked in a virtual machine on Rudolf OS's own kernel with BitLocker volumes made by Windows: AES-XTS (Windows 10 and 11), AES-CBC, and AES-CBC with the older Elephant diffuser. Each opened read-only with its recovery key, which is stored nowhere. Two fixes: opening no longer waits for ever for the system's device manager, and a mistyped recovery key now says "That key does not open it." instead of "BitLocker could not be opened here".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: a new installation now starts with the Native desktop (the owner's decision, 2026-11-22). Chromium and Lite stay in Settings › System health › Desktop engine; if Native does not start, Chromium is used. A computer updated from 1.6.1 keeps the desktop it had.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: the title bars check (std-titlebars-check.yml) passes: Chrome is started without --enable-automation, whose bar on the runner moved the desktop page 56 px down so the test's presses missed (38/38 and 22/22 now).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: the plan (docs/plan-1.6.2.md Part 31): zstd compression for the system's images, measured against today's xz in QEMU and on the owner's two computers before anything changes; the kernel learns to read zstd first.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: a Library game's save record may now be up to 6 MB (it was 256 KB), so a game with a large world, such as Ember Reach's shared galaxy, can keep it in a few records. Saves stay per package, game and account, mirrored and backed up as before. The desktop tells a game its limit when it starts, so a game made for this works on older versions too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Flatpak apps that Rudolf OS installs may now show their progress on their taskbar buttons. Each one gets a single extra permission, set by Rudolf OS, to say its progress to the desktop, and nothing else. Apps installed earlier get it at the next Update all. (Chromium-based browsers and most Electron apps today send their progress only on Ubuntu's old Unity desktop with its library inside the app. Rudolf OS cannot provide either, so they still show none; Firefox already does. See docs/plan-1.6.2.md Part 25b.)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: on the Chromium desktop, an app's own title bar and buttons work as on Native (docs/plan-1.6.2.md Part 29). Dragging an app's own title bar or edges (Discord, Steam, VS Code, GTK apps with a header bar) moves and sizes it with Rudolf's frame following, the same way and with the same limits as on Native; its own maximize button and a double-click on its bar maximize and restore it, and its own minimize button minimizes it, as Rudolf's title bar does. The app's Move and Size from the keyboard work too. Before, these did nothing on Chromium.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: the Standard desktop is now called Chromium (it is the same desktop: the desktop page in Rudolf's Chromium), and Settings › System health › Desktop engine lists the three as Native, Chromium, Lite. A computer on Standard stays on it and shows it as Chromium; nothing saved changes. Help, System health, the self-test, the sign-in's messages and rudolf-fetch say Chromium too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: the Several monitors check failed on every run although its tests passed: monbeh_t.js named a picture "cmp.lock:cover2.diff.png", and GitHub's upload of the pictures refuses a ':' in a file name. Nothing in Rudolf OS changed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: the Lite engine check's apps' own title bars test (csd161_t.sh, 7) failed whenever it ran after 18:00 UTC: with no theme chosen the native desktop turns dark at night, and the window's edge is then the dark theme's, as it should be. The test now chooses the light theme. Nothing in Rudolf OS changed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Safer: no script from another site ever runs in the desktop's page or an app window, which hold the key to the system's own service. Lua (Command Prompt, BlockLua Builder, Blitzen) always uses Rudolf's own copy of its runtime, never one downloaded from a website, and the page now has a security policy that refuses any other site's script. Flash content plays in a sealed-off frame of its own: the Flash Player app, and Oracle's pages for Flash files.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: closing Steam's window left Steam running out of sight (it goes to a tray icon, and Rudolf OS has no tray), using memory until it was force quit. When its last window is closed, and no game of it is running, Steam is now asked to quit as it quits itself, and ended if it has not after 30 s; signing out also asks it to quit first (docs/plan-1.6.2.md Part 14, found on the owner's Vivobook). Task Manager's Force quit is unchanged.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Faster: on the native desktop a Linux app such as Steam is started as soon as Rudolf knows it, instead of after every list of apps (the Library's, the Linux apps', Debian's) one after another and the Start menu's pictures, which took about 10 seconds on a slow laptop; the list of installed Linux apps is kept and given again at once until an app is installed, updated or removed; and the desktop's icons and Start menu no longer wait minutes for Linux apps' pictures that cannot be had.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Linux apps' progress on their taskbar buttons (docs/plan-1.6.2.md Part 25b). A Linux app with a download or other work in progress shows it on its taskbar button while its window is minimized (on Chromium: while another window or the desktop is in front), with the same fill as Rudolf's own windows and the same Display Properties › Taskbar › Progress colour, on Chromium and on the native desktop alike. Apps that say it with the Unity launcher signal (Chromium-based and Electron apps, and others) are heard by your account's own portal on your account's own session bus; Firefox's own progress on its window (the XApp hint) is read from the window itself. Only your own apps, and a Flatpak app only if it may talk to com.canonical.Unity and only for its own desktop file. A percentage only: the creeping fill stays for Rudolf's own work.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: the Blitzen knows check's "⚡ Why?" test (bzwhy57_t.js, 4) failed at some times of day: when the search, which reads the log lines with their times, found two pieces of one document's section, both had the same name, and the test took the one kept for the one unticked. It now unticks a row by its place and looks for that row's text. Blitzen leaves out what is unticked, as it did; nothing in Rudolf OS changed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: Oracle's status line kept saying "Goes To: <address>" after the mouse left one of Oracle's own pages (its home page, the reader) for the rest of the desktop or Oracle's own bar: Chromium does not tell such a page that the mouse left it, so the desktop now ends it itself when the mouse arrives on its own page.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Rudolf's title bar on the Chromium desktop's windows from outside the page (docs/plan-1.6.2.md Part 29, the owner, 2026-11-21): Linux apps, the encrypted Oracle and Oracle's Tor windows get the same title bar, buttons, edges and window menu as Rudolf's own windows (and as Native's frames), in the title-bar style and colour chosen in Display Properties. Drag the title bar to move them, any edge or corner to size them; maximize and restore, minimize (the taskbar button brings them back), close (the app is asked, as by its own close button), Always on top and the workspaces from the window's menu. A click on the desktop or another window puts the app behind it, its window keeping its place with the app's name ("Click to show it"). Full-screen videos and games keep the whole screen with no frame; dialogs open in the middle of their window. Chromium-based windows (the encrypted Oracle, Tor windows, Chromium-based browsers) leave their own frame off; apps that always draw their own (Steam, Discord) show both, as on Native.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop, Task Manager could come up as an empty window for several seconds (or not at all) while the desktop was busy, for example while Steam was starting: its page waited for the desktop's hidden background page. Task Manager now has a page of its own and comes up at once (docs/plan-1.6.2.md Part 14, found on the owner's Vivobook).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: two-player games from the Rudolf OS Library on your home network (docs/plan-1.6.2.md Part 30; Ember Reach 0.5.2's duels). Press Host on this network in the game, and Rudolf OS runs a small relay on this computer while you play, and announces it on the network; on the other computer Find games lists it, and the two games meet through it. Nothing goes over the internet. The relay runs as your account's own user (never as root), answers only the local network, and the firewall opens its port to the home network only (never on a cellular connection) and only while a game is hosted. It stops when the duel ends, or within a minute if no game connects.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Bring your files (docs/plan-1.6.2.md Part 27). Installing Rudolf OS on a disk that holds another system now looks at it first, read-only: Windows (each person's Documents, Pictures, Music, Videos, Desktop and Downloads, OneDrive's folders too), Linux (/home and its own folder names) and macOS (said: Rudolf OS cannot read a Mac's disk, and how to copy the files on the Mac first), each folder with its size. Keep them (the default), choose which, or erase without keeping (said with the size that is lost). Kept files are copied onto a USB drive and every one is read back and checked (SHA-256) before anything is erased; a drive that fills up is followed by another; a copy that fails or is cancelled erases nothing, and the installer itself refuses the disk until the copy (or the choice to erase) is made. A BitLocker disk asks for its recovery key (it is opened read-only and the key is never kept); a Windows that was hibernated or not shut down fully is read read-only and said. After the first sign-in Rudolf OS offers to bring them in (Settings › Update and recovery › Bring in files from the old computer): the old

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.2 (in progress)
docs.t: Documents into Documents and so on, into your own encrypted folder, names that clash kept side by side, each file checked again and then by the antivirus. The copy on the drive is left as it is.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: on Standard, with "Keep my websites encrypted with my account" on, Oracle would not open ("Oracle needs Rudolf's Chromium with its shell, which this computer does not have"): the list it starts from was only made on Native.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: File Explorer to the desktop (docs/plan-1.6.1.md Part 28, the owner, 2026-11-21): items dragged from a File Explorer window (one, or several chosen with the selection box, Ctrl or Shift) and dropped on the desktop go into your Desktop folder, as a drop on a File Explorer window would put them there: from C: moved (copied with Ctrl), from a USB drive, the Games folder or a folder of this computer by File Explorer's checked transfer with its progress window (a read-only place's files copied), names that clash named as File Explorer names them (NAME - COPY.EXT). The icons appear where they were dropped (the first in the cell under the pointer, the others next to it) and keep that place. Dropped on a desktop folder's icon they go into that folder, on the Trash into the Trash. After Cut or Copy in File Explorer (its menu, the toolbar, Ctrl+X/C), the desktop's right-click menu has Paste (greyed while nothing is cut or copied), and Ctrl+V on the desktop pastes too: the icons where the menu was opened; Cut moves and empties the clipboard, Copy copies and keeps it. A desktop folder's menu has Paste into folder, a desktop file's Cut

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: and Copy (one clipboard: Paste in File Explorer takes them). On Standard, Lite and Native alike: on Native the shell takes the drop from the Explorer window, whose page does the transfer, and gives the icons their places; its menus' Paste, Cut, Copy and Paste into folder are the page's. Fixed on Native: a click on the desktop gives it the keyboard, as on Standard (Ctrl+V, Delete and F2 on the desktop went to the window in front before). however (social engineering, a page, file, mail or log that tells it to, a key split up, spelled out, encoded or in a code block). rudolfd hides them in what Blitzen is given and in what it writes, before any of it is shown, spoken, kept or from reading key files. A password or a code is sent only after you allow it in the desktop's own prompt, which only your own click can answer. A program Blitzen runs sees only its own folder, with no network. Each attempt is in System health › Security.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: code Blitzen writes can no longer act with the desktop's rights. JavaScript and Lua it writes run in a sandbox with no access to the desktop's page, its storage, rudolfd or the network (before, a program "checked by running it" could read the desktop's page and use the system's API: something Blitzen read, a web page or a file, could have made it write one). Lua runs on a copy of your own files: a check throws the copy away; ▶ Run asks, in the desktop's own dialog, before keeping what it changed, listing each file, and only in your own folder. An HTML answer's preview loads nothing from anywhere.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: in Blitzen's answers, only the pages its web search read and Rudolf OS's own documents open with a click; any other address is shown whole and opens only after "Open this address?", which shows its site and what it would send.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: what "Learn from what I do" keeps (what you did, your notes for Blitzen, the setting itself) is kept only in your account's own encrypted folder, only while you are signed in, never for another account; what 1.6.0 kept outside it is moved in. Blitzen's model engine no longer can save a conversation to the disk.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: Developer mode: every command Blitzen proposes for your test computer is shown whole before it is sent, with what is risky in it said in plain words; one command at a time; one carrying a password, token or key is never sent. A workflow to start shows its file, and a pull request its whole change, before Allow.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: a minimized window's taskbar button shows the work it is doing: the button fills from its left edge to its right, a few pixels inside its edge and behind its picture and title, as a progress bar (a download, a page loading in Oracle, a copy or move in File Explorer, a drive's copy, Extract here, an installation or update, printing, a text message being sent, and any progress bar in the window). Work with no percentage creeps towards the end and completes when it is done; the fill fades away then, and restoring the window hides it. Green as it comes: Display Properties › Taskbar › Progress colour has Blue, Orange, Purple, Red, the accent colour and any colour. The same on Standard, Native and Lite.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: Find printers finds network printers with the firewall on (found on a Vivobook: it listed none). It now asks the network as other computers do (multicast DNS from its own port, 5353), and the firewall lets in only those answers, from the local network and never on a cellular connection; nothing else is opened. Printers that answer only to the computer that asked are found too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Changed: Settings' pages are built from one list of additions each, in the same order as before, instead of a function wrapped up to 15 times. They look and work as they did; a section that fails no longer stops the sections after it from being shown (the failure is written to the console).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: For the phone build to come (2.0): the groundwork of its home screen's three panels: on a build marked as the mobile build, the three workspaces are panels shown full screen, switched with a swipe to the left or right on the desktop or a title bar, on Standard and Native alike. Nothing changes on computers.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Printing: a print queue for the whole computer. Linux apps print too (LibreOffice, GTK and Qt apps, lp in Debian and Flatpak apps: through the queue, as on any Linux), and Settings › Devices › Print queue shows what is printing, with Cancel for your own documents; another account's are listed without their names and cannot be cancelled by you. Printers that take only pictures of the pages get them from the queue too. USB printers' devices belong to the queue alone, and an IPP over USB printer can be reached only through it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Native: an app's window loads the desktop page without 11 modules no app of its own uses (WordPro's additions, Notey for the office apps, the Wi-Fi panel, the computer check, the SNES core's loader, the weather, Settings' search and a few more); each is read the moment something of it is needed. Settings, Task Manager, Oracle, the App Store, Blitzen and the games and office apps that use them keep the whole page, as Standard and Lite do. Measured: no difference in memory that can be told from the noise (about 1 MB at most).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Native: each app's window uses about 10 MB less memory. A window no longer makes the pictures of the start menu, the desktop's icons and the taskbar for itself (the native desktop draws those), nor the taskbar's pinned buttons or the dynamic background's moving parts under the app, and it no longer gives the desktop its list of apps again when it opens if the list is unchanged. On the test computer, five app windows and the hidden page: 483 MB instead of 531 MB.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Native: the window's menu of an app that draws its own title bar says whether it can use Rudolf's instead. For apps whose own bar holds only the title and the three buttons, "Title bar: Rudolf's" cuts their own bar away and frames them as any other window, remembered for each account and app; for others the menu says Rudolf's would hide their menus and buttons.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Native: one title bar for apps that draw their own. Discord, Steam, Claude, VS Code and other Electron and Chromium apps, and GTK 3 and 4 apps with a header bar, no longer get Rudolf's title bar above their own: their window keeps Rudolf's edge, round corners and resize edges, and their own bar does the rest, as on Standard. Moving them by their bar, resizing them from any edge or corner, their maximize, restore and minimize buttons, a double-click on their bar, the keyboard's Move and Size from their window menu, and a right-click on a GTK header bar (the window's menu) all work, with the same limits and transitions as Rudolf's own title bar. GTK's invisible shadow margins are cut away. Every other window keeps Rudolf's title bar as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New (docs/plan-1.6.1.md Part 19): game mode does more, on Standard and Native alike. While a game is full screen the processor is asked for its full speed (AMD's amd_pstate and Intel's intel_pstate; not with battery saver), and behind a Linux game the desktop's own work waits (its processor time lowered, its animations stopped); notifications are held and one says how many came after, as before. Everything goes back as it was when the game leaves full screen or ends, a crash included. Games that ask for Feral's GameMode (gamemoderun, Steam's launch option, Flatpak games through the portal) get the processor's speed, and nothing else. Settings › System health › Memory › Game mode turns it all off and on.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Apps that can use the system's title bar are asked to, once: the first time Rudolf OS starts Chromium, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi, Chrome or ungoogled Chromium from Flathub, Debian's Chromium, VS Code or VSCodium, it turns on their "use the system title bar" setting, so they get Rudolf's title bar with nothing lost. Only when you have not chosen otherwise in the app; your other settings are kept.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Native: idle windows give their memory back. Notepad or File Explorer minimized, or hidden behind another window, for a while (Settings › System › Idle windows: on by default on computers with under 6 GB of memory, after 10 minutes) is closed behind the scenes and comes back where it was when you show it: its files, tabs, folder, the scroll and the window's size and place. Never with unsaved changes, a dialog, sound or video playing, a call, a download or a transfer; Oracle and Linux, Debian, Flatpak and Wine apps are never touched. Task Manager shows such a window as "Resting (no memory used)".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: Oracle blocks ads and trackers. A shield 🛡 in the address box says how many were blocked on the page; its menu turns blocking off (or on) for that site and can note a broken site in System health. Settings › Privacy › Ads and trackers in Oracle: on (the default) or off, the sites it is off for, and sites of your own to block. Private and Tor windows always block. It uses Rudolf OS's own list of well-known ad and tracking services, checked on this computer: nothing about the pages you visit is sent anywhere. On Standard, Native and Lite.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: The desktop page is 870 KB smaller: the Quake engine and the Galaxy Map's universe are files of their own, read only when Quake or the Galaxy Map opens (every window of the native desktop, and Standard's page, parsed them before). Each window of the native desktop uses about 5 MB less memory.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Native: the shell's hidden pages are one. The desktop's service page, the portal's page (a Linux or Flatpak app's questions, file dialogs and links) and the start-up page (the notice after an update) were three pages each loading the whole desktop; now one page does what each did. The quick settings' switches, Do not disturb and Clear all, pinning, muting from the taskbar, the desktop's menus, renaming, dropping onto the Trash, files dropped from Linux apps and the start menu's search are done by that page at once, instead of a page of the whole desktop loaded for each. Less memory (on the test computer 110 MB instead of 170 MB with no window open, and no 100 MB peak for each switch).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: signing in and out with your files on the disk (the encrypted folder opened with your key, your Oracle folder, Linux apps' folders, your account's own Linux user's session) and opening the encrypted folder of Settings › Security (and preparing the drive for it) are done by the drives helper as root, no longer by rudolfd, which reads every request of the desktop: the key goes to it on a pipe, never as an argument, and the account is checked again there (a removed account is refused). Nothing changes on screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: the accounts' own Linux users (made and removed with the accounts, written into the system's user list, their folders given to them) and Settings › Privacy › Saved passwords for apps are handled by a helper of their own, no longer by rudolfd; it is asked only when an account comes or goes. Nothing changes on screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: restart, shut down, sleep, the power settings, brightness, Task Manager's "Clear cache" and the desktop's priority, and setting the clock are done by a power helper of its own, no longer by rudolfd. Nothing changes on screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: Wi-Fi (scan, join, forget, the radios and bands, the country, the adapter), an address by DHCP or a fixed one and the name server, the firewall, the hotspot and metered connections are handled by a network helper of its own, no longer by rudolfd; a network's password reaches it on its standard input only. Nothing changes on screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: Bluetooth (turning it on and off, searching, pairing, connecting, forgetting, the pairing question) and Thunderbolt and USB4 devices (approving, not approving, forgetting) are handled by a devices helper of its own, no longer by rudolfd. Nothing changes on screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: Task Manager's End process and End process tree, and reading the kernel's messages (System health, the crashes list), are handled by two small helpers of their own, no longer by rudolfd. Nothing changes on screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: the display's settings (the graphics path, the desktop's shell, resolution and frame rate, the keyboard's layout, restarting the display or the desktop's browser) and sound (the volume, the microphone, the echo canceller, the sound card) are handled by helpers of their own, no longer by rudolfd. Nothing changes on screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: rudolfd can be confined (off by default until a beta has run with it: /persist/etc/rudolf-confine, or rudolf.confine= at the start-up, off, log or on). All of rudolfd loses the system calls and capabilities nothing it starts needs; each request that starts no program is put in a narrow confinement of its own (only rudolfd's own system calls, writing only in rudolfd's folders through Landlock, which the kernel now has, fewer capabilities); each of rudolf-rootd's helpers gets only its own capabilities; and the API answers each window only what its code asks for (the native shell, the page). Refusals are said in System health.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: a ZIP larger than 1.5 MB in Downloads (kept on the disk) opens in Archive Manager, which lists what is inside it (names, sizes, folders; the first 3,000 shown) without loading it, with Extract here; File Explorer's Open with offers Archive Manager for it too. Extract here (there, or in File Explorer) unpacks it next to the ZIP with a progress window (the file, n of N, the bytes, Cancel): a folder named after the ZIP, its sub-folders as in the ZIP, each file kept on the disk and checked by the antivirus (one quarantined or blocked is said so). The ZIP is unpacked as the desktop user, never as root; one with entries that point outside it ("..", an absolute path) is refused, and links in it are left out.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Changed: files kept on the disk can now be in sub-folders of Downloads, where they stay (before, they were moved back to the top of Downloads); only those at the top are renamed on the disk when renamed. Deleting them, the Trash and Downloads' own files work as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: reader mode in Oracle. On a page with an article (a news story, a blog post, a recipe) a 📖 button shows in the address box; it, F9 (also inside a website) or ☰ › Reader mode shows the article alone: its title, author and text, its pictures and links, in Rudolf's reading style, with A− A+, the width, the font (serif, sans, OpenDyslexic), light, sepia or dark (dark with Rudolf's dark theme), 🔊 Read aloud in Rudolf's own voice (the sentence being read highlighted) and 🖨 Print (the article alone). ✕ Exit reader or F9 gives the page back as it was. Nothing of the website runs in reader mode. Also for .HTM files on C:. On Standard, Native and Lite. It uses Mozilla's Readability (Apache License 2.0).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: the release build no longer stops when linux-firmware updates a file: it takes linux-firmware at the commit the firmware list was made from (the list's new "R" line), and a check runs that fetch on every change to the list.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Changed: Oracle › ☰ › Reopen my tabs next time now brings back every Oracle window you had, the tabs asleep (💤, loaded when clicked) except the one in front, so Oracle starts quickly. After Oracle or the desktop ended unexpectedly, the next Oracle window offers "Restore your tabs?" once, even with the setting off. Your tabs are kept in your own encrypted home folder (locked when you sign out), no longer in the desktop's settings. Never for private or Tor windows, or Guest.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Changed: Native uses less memory: each window's page frees its caches and collects garbage sooner (a limit that follows the computer's memory, checked every 5 s instead of 15), and the pages the desktop opens by itself at start-up wait until the others have started, so their memory peaks no longer come all at once.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: Emu's "Open a file…" refused a ZIP or disc over 512 MB ("copy it in Files instead"). A ZIP or a disc image (.chd, .cdi, .gdi, .cue, .pbp, N64) chosen there is now added to the game library (a ZIP is unpacked) and the game added starts; nothing that large is read into the page. A 7-Zip file is refused with a reason.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Changed: the most a "choose a file" window takes into an app at once follows the computer's memory: about a sixth of it (no more than 40% of what is free at that moment, and never over 2 GB) instead of 512 MB for every computer. The Vivobook (3.3 GB) keeps about 512 MB; 8 GB about 1.2 GB; 16 GB and more 2 GB. The message says why a file is too large.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: File Explorer moves files by dragging them from one window to another, between Rudolf OS's own folders, a plugged-in drive and the Games (Emu library) folder, either way: dropped on a window's list they go into the folder it shows, dropped on a folder into that folder, and what will take them is highlighted. A drag moves; Ctrl+drag copies (the pointer shows which). Cut, Copy and Paste in the right-click menu work the same between windows and drives. A move between Rudolf OS and a drive is a copy that is checked first; the originals go only once everything arrived, and one that is cancelled or fails leaves them where they were.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: a selection box in File Explorer: press on an empty spot of the list and drag over the files to select them (Ctrl or Shift adds to what is selected); then drag them, or right-click them. A drive's files can now be selected with Shift+click too, and have a right-click menu (Cut, Copy, Paste, Delete, Copy into Rudolf OS, Properties).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: a window shows a transfer's progress: the file, how many of how many, the bytes, the time left, and Cancel. It closes by itself when done and stays to say what went wrong if something did.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: copying a large download kept on the disk (Copy and Paste in Downloads) made a 99-byte "- COPY" that did not open. The copy is now a file of its own on the disk; copies made like that before are mended when Downloads is opened (kept, never deleted).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: File Explorer's Properties window showed only an icon.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: Oracle's status line (bottom left, where it says "Done") shows where a link goes while the mouse is over it: "Goes To: <address>". It covers links, image-map areas, a form's submit button and links in ads and other frames, on websites and Oracle's own pages; then the status line goes back to what it said. On Standard, Native and Lite.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: find in page in Oracle. Ctrl+F (or F3, Ctrl+G, or ☰ › Find in page…) opens a bar under the bookmarks bar: type and the matches are highlighted, "3 of 17" says where you are, Enter (or ▼, F3) goes to the next and Shift+Enter (or ▲, Shift+F3) to the previous one, round at the ends; Match case; Escape or ✕ closes it. Ctrl+F inside a website opens Oracle's bar, as in Chrome, even on sites that use Ctrl+F themselves. Text selected on the page fills the box, and the bar belongs to its tab. On websites, Oracle's own pages and files, on Standard, Native and Lite.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: after a click into a website in Oracle, Ctrl+F and Ctrl+L gave the bar or the address box the look of having the keyboard while what was typed still went to the website.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: Oracle's Downloads page shows a progress bar for a file that is arriving (how much so far and how fast, and with a known size the percentage and the time left) and one being checked. Each download has Remove beside Open: a file in Downloads goes to the Trash with it; otherwise the notification "File removed from list: Not in Downloads. Ask Blitzen if you need help finding this file." has a "⚡ Ask Blitzen" button. Blitzen reads the download's record, the Trash and where files of that name are, and says whether the file was moved, put in the Trash, deleted or never downloaded.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: reopen a closed tab in Oracle. Ctrl+Shift+T (also inside a website) or ☰ › Reopen closed tab brings back the last tab you closed, at its place and with its back and forward pages; again, the one before. ☰ › Recently closed… lists the last 25; a closed window is one entry that brings its tabs back in a window of their own. The list is kept in memory only, never written anywhere: it is forgotten when Oracle's last window closes and when you sign out. Private and Tor windows keep their own list, which goes with the window. On Standard, Native and Lite.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: Make a Rudolf OS USB stick on an older Rudolf OS stick said "/dev/sdb is in use (mounted at /run/rudolf/stkinfo-sdb/i). Unmount it first." Settings' look at what such a stick holds left its image mounted when the stick had no third partition. It now always unmounts, never looks while a stick is being made, and Make the stick unmounts a look left behind by 1.6.0.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: Make a Rudolf OS USB stick with "The latest from the update address" stopped at once with "use POST", and so did Settings › System update › Check this address: the page asked rudolfd's address check the wrong way (a GET where it takes only a POST). Its test's stand-in now refuses a GET as rudolfd does.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: the start-up's time from power-on. System health › Last starts › "Where the time went" now begins with the time before Linux starts: the computer's firmware, the boot loader and the kernel's unpacking (from the firmware's own record, ACPI's FPDT, and the processor's counter), and ends with the whole from power-on to the desktop's answer. The health log's "the desktop was ready" line adds the time from power-on, and counts an installed computer's handover.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: Emu plays Nintendo 64 and Sega Dreamcast games, in native emulators that run on the graphics card, full screen: Rosalie's Mupen GUI (Mupen64Plus) and Flycast, free emulators downloaded once from Flathub the first time a game of theirs is played. Add games takes .z64, .n64 and .v64 games, and Dreamcast discs as .cdi or .chd files or as a .gdi with its track files (each such disc gets a folder of its own); the library has Nintendo 64 and Dreamcast tabs. A plugged-in controller works in both (they set it up themselves); Super+Esc comes back to the desktop.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: Emu plays Sega Genesis / Mega Drive and PlayStation games, in Emu itself: ClownMDEmu and PCSX-ReARMed as WebAssembly (in Emu's player package, 1.1.0, from the Rudolf OS Library). Add games takes Genesis games (.md, .gen, .smd, and a .bin that says SEGA in its header) and PlayStation discs as a .cue with its track files (a folder of its own, as a Dreamcast .gdi), a .chd (a GD-ROM .chd stays a Dreamcast disc) or a .pbp; a PlayStation BIOS file (scph*.bin) goes in PS1/BIOS and is used when it is there (without one, the PlayStation's own built-in replacement starts most games). A disc is read from the library as the game asks for it, not loaded whole. The library has Genesis and PlayStation tabs. Battery memory and the PlayStation's memory card 1 save by themselves; save states as for the other consoles.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: each console in Emu has its own buttons on the keyboard, a controller and the touchscreen: the Genesis's A B C, X Y Z and Mode; the PlayStation's ✕ ○ □ △, L1 L2 R1 R2, L3 R3 and the DualShock's two analog sticks (a controller's sticks, or J I K L for the left one). Controls lists each console's own.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: two-step sign-in with an authenticator app (docs/plan-1.6.1.md Part 17, the codes; security keys that also protect your files come later). User Settings › Sign-in options › Authenticator app: set it up with the setup key in an app such as Google or Microsoft Authenticator, Aegis or 2FAS; then signing in and unlocking ask for the app's 6-digit code after the password, on Standard and on the native desktop. A code works once; after 5 wrong attempts there is a wait (30 seconds, doubling up to 15 minutes). Security Settings › Two-step sign-in: an administrator can require it for administrators or for every account.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: each other's builds (docs/plan-1.6.1.md Part 16). Settings › Update and recovery › Update address: Check this address says whether it answers, whether its releases are complete, and whose key signs them: updates install only from this computer's key; another person's build can still go on a USB stick. Only an administrator can change the address. Get beta versions switches the address that is set between its /stable and /beta. Make a USB stick can put the update address's latest release on a stick, checked first (another person's build only after a warning). Recovery mode is always the official Rudolf OS: it is kept at the newest official stable release, and every stick gets it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Planned (docs/plan-1.6.1.md Part 15): one title bar for apps that draw their own (Discord, Steam, Claude, Chromium-based browsers) on Native: the app's own setting for the system title bar where it has one; otherwise its own bar alone, with moving, resizing and maximizing from it; Rudolf's instead by choice for apps whose bar loses nothing when cut.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Tests: the kernel tuning measured in QEMU (kernel-tuning.yml, nothing published): test kernels and base layers started in turn on one machine; the start-up's steps, wake-up latency and the page's input-to-frame time under load, memory with tabs, a game and a call at once on 3.3 GB, the power settings' fallback, the start on each kind of virtual hardware, and two builds of the kernel compared.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Tests: the checks that test the newest beta's own Chromium on GitHub's runners run again (the Oracle file check, the Tor window keys, Oracle on Native and Standard with the beta's Chromium, Blitzen knows, App links, Dark pages video): the beta's Chromium carries its own glibc at /opt/chromium/glibc, so it is now linked there before it starts (iso/qt/host/betachrome.sh); before, it stopped with "required file not found" (docs/plan-1.6.1.md Part 21).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Faster start-up: the kernel is packed with zstd instead of xz (0.6 s less before it starts, in QEMU; about twice that on an installed computer, which starts two kernels), and the wired network cards' drivers are modules loaded after the start.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: Settings › System health › Last starts › Where the time went: each step of the start-up and how long it took. The health log's "the desktop was ready N s" and Last starts now give the moment the desktop first answered (they were up to 4 s and 10 s late).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: Settings › System health › Power and battery › Processor energy preference, for AMD processors (amd_pstate): Tuned saves power on battery (balance_power) and gives a full-screen game full speed (performance); the kernel's own (passive) for comparison. As in 1.6.0 stays the default until it is measured on a laptop.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Changed: the kernel's build stops when a feature Rudolf OS relies on is missing (75 options, each with who needs it: Flatpak's sandboxes, the Debian container and Wine, the desktop, security, reaching the system disk, power); FUSE, which the x86 kernel lacked, is added (Flatpak's document portal, AppImages).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Lite desktop, a game's "Save to a file" (Ember Reach's, for one) or any file picker in a game or on a website no longer freezes the computer. WebKit asked with a file dialog that went through Rudolf OS's own portal, which draws its dialog in the desktop page, while the desktop's window was held for that dialog: nothing could be clicked or typed, Task Manager opened behind it, and only the power button got out (the Vivobook, 2026-11-17). A save from the desktop page now goes to Downloads, as a website's download does, and a file picker (Load from a file, a site's upload in Oracle) is the desktop's own Open dialog. Should the Lite desktop itself ever ask the portal for a file dialog again, the portal answers "cancelled" at once instead.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed: smart cards were never seen (1.6.0). OpenSC's card module could not start, because pcsc-lite's client library (libpcsclite.so.1, which OpenSC loads itself) was missing from the system. So Settings › Smart cards always said no reader was plugged in, and Oracle never offered a card's certificates. It is in the system now. Found by the new virtual smart card test (docs/plan-1.6.1.md Part 21).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Tests: a virtual PIV smart card with a test CA made by the test (iso/qt/host/vpiv.py). On the host it uses vsmartcard's virtual reader, OpenSC, the smartcard script and NSS. In QEMU it uses the newest beta's own reader stack, through QEMU's USB CCID reader: the reader plugged in, Settings › Smart cards, Oracle signing in to a test site with Chromium's certificate picker and PIN box, a Tor window without the card, the screen locked when the card is taken out (smartcard-qemu-check.yml; nothing is published).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: User Settings › Sign-in options › Authenticator app shows the setup link as a QR code beside the setup key, so a phone's authenticator app adds the account with its camera (an encoder of Rudolf OS's own; dark on white with its margin in every theme). On Standard, Native and Lite.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New: security keys that protect your files (User Settings › Sign-in options › Security keys). Rudolf OS reads FIDO2 keys itself on Standard, Native and Lite: after your password, touch one of your keys. Add two (one as a spare) and "Require a security key": then a copy of your disk opens nothing without your password and one of your keys together. Old security keys checked by the sign-in screen only are moved over when you add your keys again. What to do if keys are lost: docs/security-keys.md.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Security: Standard's websites (and Native's Oracle) in the shared browser profile, with "Keep my websites encrypted with my account" off, are now encrypted with a key kept in the computer's security chip (TPM 2.0) and tied to its Secure Boot, in place of the browser's built-in key: the drive taken out of the computer, or another system started on it, cannot read the sign-ins, saved site passwords and cards. Without a TPM, as before. Turning Secure Boot off or on makes a new key once: websites ask you to sign in again. Settings › Oracle › Website data says which way it is kept.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Lite: the desktop's menus and windows now open over Oracle's tabs instead of behind their pages. While something covers part of a tab, a still picture of the page is shown there (taken again every 2 seconds); the page itself goes on running and is back as soon as nothing covers it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Lite: with the graphics card set to "Use it for games and Linux apps" (the default), Oracle's tabs are now drawn by the graphics card while the desktop itself stays drawn by the processor, for smoother scrolling, games and videos in tabs.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: New (docs/plan-1.6.1.md Part 19): NVIDIA's own graphics driver, by choice, for GeForce 16 and newer: Settings › Display › Graphics driver, "Open (NVK)" (the default) or "NVIDIA's driver" (NVIDIA's open kernel modules and its OpenGL and Vulkan libraries, a signed system extension from Settings › Update and recovery › System extensions; its modules signed for Secure Boot like the kernel's own, checked by the kernel). If it cannot be used (a module refused, Xorg not starting, the desktop not coming up), the computer goes back to the open driver by itself and says so. Recovery mode always uses the open driver.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Several monitors, the system's part (plan Part 1): every monitor plugged in, up to three, is lit side by side, the main one at the left, as Settings › Display › Displays arranged them for that set of monitors (kept per set); plugged in or out, they are arranged again within a second. Linux apps and games open on the main monitor. (rudolf-display --arrange and --monitors, screenctl arrange, rudolfd's screen/arrange; the software display still shows one monitor.)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Several monitors on the desktop (plan Part 1), Standard and Native alike: each monitor shows one of the three workspaces, with the wallpaper and a taskbar of its own (the start button, the pinned apps, that workspace's windows, the workspaces and the clock); the main monitor keeps the tray, the desktop's icons and the Start menu. A window moved to another workspace moves to the monitor showing it, one dragged onto another monitor joins its workspace, and a maximised window fills its own monitor. A workspace's button on a monitor's taskbar shows it there. A monitor unplugged: its windows stay in their workspace and none is left off the screen. Settings › Display › Displays lists the displays and which workspace each shows, and makes another the main one. The sign-in and lock screens cover every monitor.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed (Part 19's follow-up): Settings › Display › Graphics driver offers NVIDIA's driver before its extension is installed (the list of GeForce 16 and newer cards was not in the base yet), and only for Turing and newer cards; NVIDIA's extension builds (glibc's librt.so.1 was missing).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed (Part 19's follow-up): game mode puts everything back by itself after a game crashes, also when nothing asks again (its watcher is a process of its own).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.1 (2026-11-22, release 2026112201)
docs.t: Fixed (Part 19's follow-up): a system extension with kernel modules or firmware (NVIDIA's driver) has them laid over the system again; on Rudolf OS /lib is /usr/lib, and those were taken after /usr's own overlay, one overlay too many.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Oracle's website data can be kept encrypted with your account: Settings › Oracle › "Keep my websites encrypted with my account". On, Oracle's sign-ins, site data, cache and saved site passwords go in a folder of the account's own, encrypted with the same key as its home folder and locked when it signs out. On by default on Native and Lite; off by default on Standard (Settings says plainly that off means not encrypted), where turning it on opens Oracle in a Chromium window of its own over the desktop, as Browse with Tor's windows are, using a little more memory while it is open. The choice is kept inside the account's encrypted folder, so it cannot be changed with the drive alone, and turning it off asks for the account's password. Only for accounts whose files are on the disk. The first time, the account's websites ask to sign in again, and their old unencrypted copy is removed. Tests: oraacct60_t.js 18-34, homeapi_t.sh 15a-15j.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: Settings › Volume Controls was empty for an account whose settings were saved before 1.6.0 (they had only the first ten sound categories, which replaced the whole list at sign-in). Every sound category is now filled in with its default, and the account's own choices are kept. Test: iso/qt/shell2/sounds60_t.js.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Make a stick takes USB sticks and memory cards of 1.8 GB or more (was 2 GB), so a "2 GB" stick a little short of it can be used. The room the system actually needs is still checked before anything is erased.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: The native desktop clears Oracle's websites as Chromium mode does: an account deleted in Settings has its websites cleared by Oracle (at once when Oracle is open, otherwise when it next starts), and signing out closes Oracle as it closes every other window, after saving its tabs for "Reopen my tabs next time" and clearing Guest's websites. Before, these happened only when done from Oracle's own page, and Oracle stayed open after signing out. Test: iso/qt/shell2/oraacct60_t.js 12–17.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: A USB stick made from another build of Rudolf OS (its update address, or a computer running it) now starts the official recovery system in Recovery mode: Make a stick puts the official Recovery mode start-up file (recovery.efi) of the official recovery system's release on it, from that release's boot image (its checksum and Rudolf OS's Secure Boot signature checked; kept for the next stick), and adds the boot menu's Recovery mode entry when the build has none. The build's own start is left as it is. Offline with none kept, the stick keeps the build's own and says so. With Secure Boot on, the official file starts where the computer trusts Rudolf OS's key. Test: iso/qt/host/recefi60_t.sh.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Changed: the window transitions (LitePoint) are longer: opening 240 ms (corner to corner, was 200; side to side, was 220), minimizing and closing 240 ms (were 200), maximizing and restoring 200 ms (were 180); the start menu 200 ms opening (was 160) and 160 ms folding back (was 140); the taskbar's pop-ups and right-click menus 160 ms (were 140 and 120); a window's taskbar button 120 ms (was 100).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Changed: Oracle's websites (sign-ins and site data) belong to an account's ID, not its name, so a deleted account made again with the same name starts with none; Guest's are kept in memory only and forgotten when Guest signs out; a deleted account's are forgotten. Everyone signs in to websites again once (docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 21), and is told so.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: Oracle › ☰ › Reopen my tabs next time: Oracle opens the tabs you had open when you last closed it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: smart cards, such as the DoD Common Access Card (CAC) and PIV cards (docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 20). Card readers work, and Oracle can sign in to websites with the card: it shows the card's certificates, then asks for the card's PIN (Rudolf OS never sees it). Settings › Security Settings › Smart cards shows the reader, the card and when its certificates expire; an administrator can install the DoD's certificates (downloaded from the DoD and checked against the DoD's root certificates first); and "Lock the screen when my card is taken out". Never in Tor windows. Linux programs (Debian) can use the card too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: File Explorer › a drive › Copy to another drive… copies files and folders from one drive straight onto another (a USB stick, say), folders and all, with no limit on size or number, and nothing on the first drive changed. "Only personal files" leaves out Windows, programs, AppData and system files, for rescuing an old computer's documents, pictures and videos. When the drive fills up, plug in the next one and copy again: it carries on with the rest.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Oracle's loading line (docs/plan-1.6.0.md 17c): LitePoint's point of light moves left to right along the bottom of the bookmarks bar as a page loads, lighting the line behind it; it runs to the end and fades when the page is loaded, and fades where it stopped when a load fails. LitePoint's colour and brightness; Reduce motion: a plain line that fills.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the Rudolf sounds (docs/plan-1.6.0.md 17d): a start-up chime and a shut-down chime of Rudolf OS's own, and a matching sound for each part of the desktop, as a new "Rudolf" style in every category of Settings › Volume Controls. Nine new categories, each with Classic, Retro, Candy, Minimal and Rudolf: signing out and locking, an update ready, warnings (the questions before something that cannot be undone), the battery low (once at 10 %), a device connected and removed, the start menu, the Trash emptied and a screenshot. "Use one style everywhere" picks one style for all 18, the nearest each older category has. The native desktop plays the same samples as Standard. The sounds you have chosen stay as they are.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on a slow computer the Lite (and Native) desktop could be given up as "no answer in 90 s" while it was still starting (QEMU's ARM64 check: Lite answered at 82-95 s, then fell back to Standard). A desktop still busy starting (more than a fifth of a processor in the last 10 s) is now given until 300 s; one that is idle and silent is still given up at 90 s.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: For your own builds (docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 19): a build knows the repository it comes from (/etc/rudolf/origin, written by its workflow): a fork's computers take Get beta versions, Blitzen's model, Debian's base, Make a stick's boot files and the release downloads from the fork, file system reports on it, and the development link's put takes its releases; Settings › About names it. The recovery system and Return to official Rudolf OS stay official.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Blitzen looks things up before it answers (docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 18): in Rudolf OS's own source and documents (the running release's, fetched once while the computer is idle, on mains power or a battery at 50 % or more and not on a metered connection; every system release now carries its source, in its signed list), in the system's logs (passwords, tokens and keys left out) and in notes you ask it to keep ("Remember that …"); each answer lists what it used, a source file opening at its line. "Look it up first" can be turned off in the chat. "Search the web" (off, and off again after each question) sends only the question (DuckDuckGo, as Oracle searches; through Tor if asked) and reads the first pages, numbered and opened in Oracle. Settings › Apps › Blitzen: what it knows: "Learn from what I do on this computer" (off at first, per account: the apps and files opened, by name, the settings changed, the errors met; kept on this computer only), Memory, and "See what Blitzen knows" to forget an item, a day or everything. It does not retrain its model.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed (2026-11-18, the owner's Vivobook, Standard): saving from Oracle (a Gmail attachment) froze the desktop: Oracle's tabs are the desktop browser's own, so the Save dialog it asked for was drawn in the desktop's page while Chromium held that window for it; nothing answered, and Task Manager came up behind it. rudolf-portal now saves what the desktop's own browser asks to save straight to Downloads (under its name, another if taken) and says so in a notification; an Open it asks for is cancelled (never drawn over itself), as the Lite desktop's already were. portal60_t.sh 6a-6c.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed (2026-11-17, the owner's Vivobook): Discord (and other Flatpak apps that start their own processes through Flatpak's portal, as Electron apps do) showed no window when run as the account's own Linux user: the account's session bus was started with no environment, so Flatpak's portal, which the bus starts on demand, had no XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and could not find the running app ("Could not find requesting pid"). The bus now starts with the session's settings (rudolfd-users.inc; keyring60_t.sh 4b).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Window transitions "Splitting–Merging LitePoint" (the owner's design, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 17): points of light draw a window's frame as it opens (corner to corner 200 ms; side to side 220 ms for a window another window opened), grow it to maximize (180 ms), drop it into its taskbar button to minimize (200 ms; backward to restore), gather it to restore (180 ms) and fold it away to close (200 ms), meeting in a red spark; the same on Standard (desktop/litepoint60.js, in place of the fade) and Native (the same scenes in iso/sys/litepoint.h; X shapes and small windows of its own, no compositor; the window resized once). Display Properties › Colours and theme: "The window transitions (LitePoint)" in the accent colour (Normal, Negative, Complementary; white when not ticked) and their light from Off to full. None with Reduce motion. Tests: iso/qt/shell2/litepoint60_t.js (the page and the native scenes compared), native59_t.sh 28b–45b. 1.6.0b is the public beta; the finished release drops the b.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: LitePoint for the start menu (160 ms opening from the start button, 140 ms folding back into it), the taskbar's pop-ups (140 ms, from above the button clicked), right-click menus (120 ms, from their corner at the pointer) and a window's taskbar button when switching to it (100 ms, its outline): moving away from the taskbar's side (up from a bottom taskbar, down from a top one, sideways from one at the side), the menus where they were (docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 17b). Minimizing clears toward the taskbar's side too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop a new desktop icon (New folder, New text document, a file saved to the Desktop folder, a tick in Desktop icons…) could take minutes to appear: when several windows gave the desktop's list at the same moment, all but one were refused ("could not save"), and the account's own copy was not kept. Each is kept now; the log says when the icons came after signing in.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W and Ctrl+N in Oracle's website tabs did nothing when the desktop was busy for a moment (Ctrl was let go before the desktop passed the key on); they now work as on Standard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: File Explorer's Drives list shows another Rudolf OS stick (its data, read-only, as "Rudolf OS data (another Rudolf OS, read-only)"), and no longer lists the system's own internal devices (dm-0, dm-1, ...) as drives.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: a new USB stick (Make a USB stick) or a new installation (Install here) no longer stops at the Native desktop's sign-in screen with no account: until Rudolf OS is set up, it starts on Standard, whose setup wizard makes the first account, and Native from the next start.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: Recovery mode, nomodeset and rudolf.nogpu=1 start without the graphics card's driver again: udev's drivers-by-modalias rule (#465) no longer loads it at start-up.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: the built-in microphones of AMD laptops whose microphones are on the AMD audio processor (the ASUS Vivobook Go E1404FA and others) work again; since udev replaced mdev in 1.6.0, drivers for devices that appear after start-up (here the processor's microphone devices) were no longer loaded, so Settings › Sound listed only the headset jack's microphone and nothing was heard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: every release promoted to stable is also published as an install release (the .iso, the boot image, their checksums, README.TXT, the source, and a new INSTALL.TXT with the steps to install), marked Latest on the Releases page; betas no longer take the Latest mark.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: betas again come with their boot image (boot.iso: Make a stick, Put back the official start-up files, Rufus sticks); since 2026-11-17 the release workflow no longer found the disc release it is made from among the newest 50 releases, so 2026111707 to 2026111712 had none.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Changed: the boot image's menu (an installed drive's start-up files after Get new boot files or a repair, and a stick made from boot.iso) says "Start Rudolf OS" again, not "Start Rudolf OS (boot files: the system installed on this drive)"; a stick with nothing installed still says so as it starts. The firmware's boot list is unchanged ("Rudolf OS").

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on computers whose firmware does not start a drive named only by itself (the ASUS Vivobook's AMI firmware), Rudolf OS's boot entry now names the drive, its start-up files and \EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI, as the firmware's own setup does; before, beta 2026111711 could write the drive alone, and the computer opened its setup screen at the next start.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Security: what rudolfd does as root for drives (mounting, unmounting and ejecting a USB drive or SD card, a stick's information, Install, Make a stick, Replace the boot files, Keep files on this drive) is now done by a small helper that checks every name and file again itself (a disc image must really be in your home folder, yours or the signed-in account's), run by rudolf-rootd, which only rudolfd can ask. Nothing changes in how the desktop works; it is the first step towards rudolfd no longer running as root.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Security: system updates (checking, downloading, rolling back, going back to stable, Return to official, Developer mode, the update settings) go through a helper of their own the same way, which checks again what rudolfd is asked.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop an app's window appears once, at its own size, with its app in it (opening as on Standard), instead of first showing Rudolf's sign-in screen or the desktop page in a large window before shrinking to the app; an app that is slow to start appears after 2.5 s as a plain window of its colour until it is ready.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop a right-click menu replaced by another (a second right-click elsewhere, on the desktop, an icon or the taskbar), or the start menu, a tray pop-up or the indicator replaced by another, no longer leaves a strip of the first one on the screen; a right-click on the taskbar closes the start menu, as on Standard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop the desktop's icons appear at once at sign-in (each account's own from its last session, then as they are now), and a new folder or text document made from the desktop's menu, a file saved to the Desktop folder or deleted from it shows on the desktop within half a second, as in File Explorer (it took seconds, or until another window opened).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop a background, colour or other look chosen in Settings › Display Properties shows on the whole desktop at once, before Apply, and goes back on Revert or when Settings is closed without applying, as on Standard; the screen saver's Preview is full screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: about 1 keyring creation or unlock in 256 failed for Linux apps (the app told "dismissed", gnome-keyring-daemon logging "Cannot import an invalid key"): the desktop's side of the secret exchange now keeps the shared value at 192 bytes, leading zero bytes included, as gnome-keyring-daemon does.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: a start no longer rewrites the drive's start-up files by itself when they are not the official ones (it rewrote the whole area in front of your files, and on one ASUS laptop the computer then found nothing to start); it is said in System health instead.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop a file dragged from a Linux app (Debian's file manager, a Flatpak app, an AppImage) onto the desktop is copied into the Desktop folder, as on Standard (where a drop on a folder's icon or the Trash also goes to the Desktop folder, and text or the taskbar takes none); it did nothing. The file is read for the desktop by the account's own Linux user, only from the account's own files and the drives (Flatpak's document portal is mapped to the real file), never through a link; the original stays where it was.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Tests: the native desktop takes X drops from a stand-in Linux app (the desktop, a folder's icon, the Trash, a taskbar button, text, another account's file, a link out, a folder), compared with what Standard's page keeps for the same drops; rudolfd's reading of dropped files on the host (xdrop161_t.sh, drop161_t.sh).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: a computer whose start-up files were rewritten (by 1.6.0's automatic repair, or Get new boot files) could open its firmware's setup screen instead of starting: the firmware's entries for the drive (Rudolf OS's own, and one made in the firmware's setup) named where the old start-up files were, and the new ones are elsewhere.
