The "Rudolf OS" entry now follows the start-up files at every start, also from a USB stick, so starting once from a stick puts such a computer right. A new or corrected entry is written under its own number and read back before it replaces the old one, which is kept as "Rudolf OS (previous)" until a start proves the new one. Firmware settings are changed in place (never deleted first), read back, and each change is said in System health (they were refused there before, so the repair's own reports never showed). A drive whose ID Linux leaves out is named with the ID the firmware gives it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: new start-up files are put into the drive's EFI system partition one file at a time (each written beside the old one, checked, then renamed; the old ones kept until the next start from the drive), never over the drive's whole start-up area, its partition table or its signature; the firmware's entry is checked before any restart, and if anything does not check the old files are put back. This is how Get new boot files, Replace the boot files only, Return to official and the start-up's staged write work now; new boot files staged by an older version for the start-up are removed unwritten. A drive whose EFI system partition has no room (made by Rudolf OS 1.4) is left as it is, and it says so.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: Settings › Update and recovery › Start-up of this drive: "Check this drive's start-up…" (its partitions, its start-up files and their signatures, the firmware's entry for it, put right when needed; it says what it found and changed) and "Put back the official start-up files…" (only on mains power or above 50 % battery). Both need an administrator's password; Rudolf OS no longer changes the start-up files by itself.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: the self-test's "listeners" check failed on 1.6.0 with "something listens that the list of listeners does not name: unix /run/udev/control" (udev's control socket, since 1.6.0 uses udev).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: System health no longer says "the desktop's memory group is missing or empty" when the computer restarts, and the desktop's page and API stay closed to other programs while the desktop is stopped for a restart or started again (an empty group turned the check off).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop the desktop's background work runs once, whether or not any app window is open, as on Standard: an alarm or a Clock timer rings once (it did not ring with no window open, and rang once per open window), also after the Clock's window is closed; a Calendar reminder, a call's or a message's notice and Bluetooth's and Thunderbolt's questions show once; update checks, the Debian and Linux apps' updates and the session's save run once. App windows no longer each run the other apps' background work.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Changed: Oracle's start page now reads "A Chromium-based browser for Linux" under its name.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: Oracle in Rudolf's dark theme: no white strip under the page (between the page and the status bar); an open start page now follows the dark theme turning on or off by itself at dusk and dawn, not only from Settings.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop a Linux app's requests to the desktop now appear at once, above every window, whether or not any other window is open, and only once, as on Standard: the keyring's password prompts (signing in to Sober, the Roblox client, spun for ever: its "new keyring" password prompt never appeared, as nothing on Native collected it with no app window open), file Open and Save dialogs, links (in Oracle) and notifications (the desktop's own); with app windows open each of them drew the request inside itself (behind the app, or twice). The native desktop now collects them itself and shows each once. A file dialog whose app quit or was force-quit closes by itself instead of waiting, so an app opened again after a force-quit asks again at once. Task Manager's list of running apps (and its Force quit, which ends an app with all its background processes) was always empty, as its request was refused; it lists them again, so an app stuck half-closed can be ended and opened again.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: Linux apps that sign in through a web page work: "Continue with Google" in Claude's desktop app (and Discord, Steam, VS Code, Slack, Spotify) opens the page in Oracle instead of doing nothing, and after signing in the site's link back to the app (claude://…) goes to that app after Oracle asks "Open Claude?". Linux programs in Debian (and AppImages run from it) had no way to open a web page: their xdg-open, xdg-email, x-www-browser, sensible-browser, $BROWSER and GIO's default for web links now hand the link to the desktop through the Rudolf portal, as Flatpak apps' do, so web pages open in Oracle, mail in Mail and files in their app; and Oracle (Chromium on Standard and in Native's Oracle window, WebKit on Lite) gives a link of an app's own scheme to the Linux app whose launcher registers it, on Standard and Native alike. Settings › Apps › Links shows which app opens each kind of link and lets you choose another, or none; links no app registers stay refused. Also, since 1.5.9 the questions an account's own programs ask the desktop (their portal runs as the account's Linux user) could not be left for it and

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: were lost without a word: Flatpak apps' links and file dialogs did nothing while an account was signed in; they reach the desktop again, each readable by its own user only.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop Oracle's title bar and taskbar button show the page's title ("Downloads - Oracle", a site's name), as on Standard; with Rudolf's Chromium they said "Oracle" whatever the page, and a Tor window's title had no "(Tor)".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: in Oracle's website tabs other than the first, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W and Oracle's other keys did nothing and the tab showed the address instead of the page's name (both desktops).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Changed: Standard stays the default desktop for new installations in 1.6.0, and Native is not offered after an update (the owner, 2026-11-17: Native becomes the default in 1.6.1, once Discord and Steam work on it on the Vivobook); Native can be chosen in Settings › System health › Desktop engine. An update keeps the desktop the computer had.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Tests: Oracle's window on the Native desktop is compared with Standard's, part by part (title bar, tabs, toolbar, address box, bookmarks bar, the Home page, a website, the menu, downloads, dark and light mode, the accent colour) and step by step (new and closed tabs, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+N, Alt+F4, back and forward, full screen), with Rudolf's own Chromium too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Tests: Browse with Tor's keys, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+N and Ctrl+Q in a website in the Tor window, are checked as in Oracle's other windows (the tab closes, a new tab, a new Tor window, Q does nothing) on the standard and the native desktop, with a test of the screen and keyboard service's own key handling for each kind of window (the desktop, the Tor window, Oracle's and Linux apps' windows, where the keys are unchanged).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: Return to official Rudolf OS clears the custom build's system once the official one has started (the start-up dropped the return's mark when it tried the official system, so the custom build stayed on the drive). Tested in QEMU on the real release with its own boot files: the official recovery's start-up files and recovery system put back at the next starts after being changed or deleted, Return to official (and the official rudolf.efi written again), Developer mode on a computer that never ran the official build (the official recovery system downloaded), and with Secure Boot on: a custom build refused, Return to official and Recovery mode.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Changed: the repair of the start-up files waits for the network (a start whose Wi-Fi connects late no longer puts it off for a day), and a disc build stops if its EFI image would not fit an El Torito entry (32 MiB; it is 27 MiB, and the build warns from 30 MiB).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: Oracle has its own icon and start page. The icon (Stonehenge in white on navy, in a white circle) is used by Oracle's app everywhere, on Standard and Native, in every icon style and accent colour; the network's globe is unchanged. The start page shows Stonehenge under an arc: a softened navy page with the logo in white in dark mode (Rudolf's dark theme or Oracle's Dark pages, which no longer invert it), and a white page with the logo in navy in light mode. The artwork was made by Rudolf OS's owner (with GPT, after Stonehenge, an ancient monument) and traced to vector shapes.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: System health now shows what the start-up did with the signed system extensions (one left out because its file changed, its signature is not the release key's, it was built for another base or the last start with it never reached the desktop; a start script stopped after its time limit): those lines went to a health log in memory that nothing reads, because the extensions were laid over before the data partition was marked as in use. Tested in QEMU on the real release with test extensions (in use after a restart, broken ones left out, an update of the base with and without the extension's build, Roll back system, Recovery mode).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: Settings › Update and recovery › Roll back to last stable version…, shown when Get beta versions is on or when this computer runs a build the update server does not list as a published stable release (a beta, a test build, a developer's build). It says which version it goes back to and what that version does not use, asks an administrator's name and password, starts the stable release from the other system slot when it is still there (nothing to download) or downloads it as updates are, turns Get beta versions off, and restarts; on a developer's build it is Return to official Rudolf OS. Each release list now says how the release keeps your accounts and files, and going back to a release that could not read this computer's data is refused, saying why, with nothing changed (1.5.9 reads 1.6.0's data; 1.5.8 and older do not). Fixed with it: Return to official Rudolf OS on a computer without an official recovery system stopped at "another update is running".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop quick settings' switches are saved where the native desktop and every window read them, at once, so the taskbar's switches always agree with the windows (High contrast or Do not disturb could show off on the taskbar while the windows had them on); and a pop-up (quick settings, the calendar, the volume, a menu) now always catches the pointer once it is on the screen, so a click anywhere else closes it, as on Standard, also on a slower computer.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: 3D games and other Linux apps that draw with OpenGL work again (Unvanquished showed only "Couldn't load a renderer.", SuperTuxKart installed but did not start): since 1.5.9 the display server looked for the graphics drivers in a folder that does not exist, so it offered OpenGL to no program, whoever ran it (2D apps and the desktop itself were not affected). Settings › System health › Run the self-test now says when the display server offers no OpenGL to Linux apps.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: sleep on AMD laptops (the Vivobook Go's Ryzen 3 7320U): the kernel has AMD's power management controller driver (AMD_PMC, and AMD_PMF), which their modern standby needs to really sleep; and the hardware check's sleep step now passes only when the computer really slept (the kernel's own count and clocks, from rudolfd), saying why not otherwise, instead of when ten seconds had passed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: Task Manager's "Check this computer…" on the Native desktop: the sound step's tones are played once the app window's sound output is open, and "Play again" reuses it (a tone started at once could be lost); the microphone step listens for 3 s from the microphone's first sound (WebKit's takes a moment to open it); the drawing step really draws its moving picture (its two shaders gave one value different precisions, so it never linked, on Standard as on Native, and only the dark background was shown while frames were counted) and fails when nothing is drawn.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: the system report on the Native desktop describes the computer, not the window it was made in: "Pages drawn with" names the graphics chip WebKit draws with (from EGL where GTK has no OpenGL; it said "Apple GPU"), "Desktop size" is the screen's (it was Task Manager's window, 860x546), and "Desktop" says native.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: "Report a problem… › Save to a file" saves into the signed-in account's own Documents (it went to C:\DOCUMENTS, the old shared folder File Explorer no longer shows, so the file could not be found), says the full path and offers "Open the folder"; on Native the file reaches the disk at once and File Explorer's own window opens there.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop the health log's "the desktop was ready N s after start-up" counted the time the sign-in screen waited for a password (197 s on the Vivobook), as the pages there load only after signing in; the native desktop now notes it when its sign-in screen shows, with when it started and how long its screen took.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop the keyboard step of Task Manager's "Check this computer…" saw every key again (19 did not answer on the Vivobook: F1 opened Help in front of the check, Super the start menu, and the keys pressed after them went there): while the step (or Settings › Keyboard's "Press keys…") is in front, the native desktop leaves every key to it. Super is no longer kept from the apps: a lone Super still opens the start menu, and an app sees the key as on Standard (MetaLeft, Meta); the apps' windows name it as Chromium does. Only Rudolf OS's exact shortcuts are taken from the apps, so arrows, F-keys, Ctrl and Alt reach games and editors as on Standard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop the desktop's sounds play as on Standard, with the account's Volume Controls: a window opening and closing, the taskbar's buttons, the start menu's rows, menus' rows, quick settings and the pop-ups' buttons, dialogs' buttons, notifications and the sounds inside apps, each once (only the start-up, sign-in, error and shut-down chimes played before).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop the Library's apps (Ember Reach), Windows programs (Starport GE) and Linux apps (Discord, Steam, Claude) open from the start menu, the taskbar's pins and the desktop's icons as on Standard (a program rudolfd runs leaves no empty window), and the Linux and Windows programs show their own icons there; the start menu's search is Standard's (apps, Settings' pages, files, sums), so Packages is found again; Desktop icons… lists every app at once (Ember Reach was missing until "Restore the standard icons") and a tick shows or hides the icon on the desktop within a second (it took minutes, or never happened).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop an app's window no longer shows the sign-in screen for a moment before the app: the window signs in with the native session without drawing it (it still appears when a window really has to ask, such as the page opened by hand).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop the display settings (title bars, the taskbar, colours and the accent, light or dark, the background, fonts and sizes, and the rest) change the native desktop and every open app window at once, as on Standard; a window that had missed a change, or Oracle's page, can no longer put the older settings back.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop the System monitor and Weather widgets kept "CPU: –", "Memory: –", "Windows: 0" and "Loading…" for good after the native desktop started again or at an unlucky moment of signing in; they now always show live values (the monitor counts every open window, Oracle's too), or the weather's error.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop notices no longer pop up again: "Rudolf OS was updated…" shows once per account and release (from the desktop itself, not from each app window as it opened), and "Real browser tabs are ready" is no longer offered there (Oracle on Native already has real tabs; its "restart the desktop" would have started Standard's browser).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop, signing in now opens the encrypted folder (Debian, Linux and Windows programs, Linux apps, Downloads) as Standard's sign-in does, so the Terminal opens Linux (Debian) again instead of only Command Prompt (C:) tabs; Ctrl+Alt+T in an app's window opens the Terminal's own window, and the Start button's and the desktop's "Command Prompt" open the Command Prompt as on Standard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop sound from the app windows (the Media Player, games, videos) no longer stops for good once a page muted or turned down a sound: each window's sounds are mixed by it, as Chromium does, so nothing one page does is kept for the others; and the desktop's own sounds play there too: the start-up chime at the sign-in screen, the sign-in and unlock sound, the error at a wrong password and the shut-down chime, with your Volume Controls settings.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the native desktop, pressing a quick settings switch could restart the whole desktop (the page doing it offered Standard's "Real browser tabs are ready" and restarted the browser); the magnifier no longer risks ending the desktop when a window closes while it draws.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the native desktop, a new window now fades in and grows as on the standard desktop; the windows in Super+Tab's overview go on moving (a video keeps playing there); what is behind a notification (its shadow and corners) is shown as it is now, not as it was when the notification came, and a notification no longer sits 15 px off after another one goes.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the native desktop, a new window now fades in and grows as on the standard desktop; the windows in Super+Tab's overview go on moving (a video keeps playing there); what is behind a notification (its shadow and corners) is shown as it is now, not as it was when the notification came, and a notification no longer sits 15 px off after another one goes; an app's window on a smaller screen (1280×800) is no longer shorter than on the standard desktop; drop-down lists show their arrow in dark mode.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: Oracle showed a blank white page for its Welcome and README bookmarks, an .HTML file opened from File Explorer and now and then its own about: pages (Rudolf's Chromium 158 sometimes started a sandboxed page's own process as if the page were not shown); such pages are drawn again, still in their sandbox. A phone number (tel: link) clicked in a page on the drive now asks how to call it, as in Oracle's real tabs.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the native desktop, quick settings' switches now work as on Standard with app windows open: Night light and High contrast colour the whole screen (taskbar, desktop, every window and Linux apps), the magnifier zooms the whole screen round the pointer, the on-screen keyboard is one keyboard above every window that types into the window in front (it showed a keyboard inside each window), touch mode makes the title bars and the tray's buttons larger, High contrast and Touch mode are kept (they were lost, so the other windows never followed), Do not disturb holds every window's pop-ups, the screen reader says that it is on, and Settings comes to the front if it is open.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the native desktop, the power button shows the power dialog at once, above every window, and only once (it was left waiting until a page took it: Oracle drew it inside its own window minutes later); the dialog has "Restart into Windows" as on Standard, and Escape cancels it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the native desktop, the volume and brightness keys show Rudolf's indicator whichever window is in front (also when the computer's firmware changes the brightness itself), Ctrl+Alt+Del and Ctrl+Shift+Esc bring up Task Manager above every window, and Standard's other global keys work there too (the screen reader, the magnifier's zoom, a screenshot, clipboard history, the emoji panel, the next keyboard layout); the taskbar has the brightness button again.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: on the native desktop the windows' title bars and frames now look and work exactly as on the standard desktop with every setting, not only the defaults: the title follows Display Properties' font size (the bar grows with large sizes), Wireframe title bars use the window's own text colour (they were black on black in dark mode), windows not in use are dark grey in dark mode in every style, the touch mode's larger title bar and buttons, high contrast's white edge and colour vision filters, 📌 for Always on top, □ (not ❐) on a maximised window, which keeps its round corners and the standard desktop's size, and Oracle's window is dark in dark mode too; the display scaling no longer blurs edges; a right-click on a title bar opens the window's menu and a middle-click sends the window behind the others; resizing follows the standard desktop's sizes. Fixed: after the native desktop ended (given up, or started again), Oracle's Chromium kept running and held the standard desktop's profile, so the standard desktop then opened in plain Chromium windows with grey title bars of Chromium's own; it is now closed first. Settings › System health › Last starts

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: Messages, for text messages through a cellular modem: conversations, read and send (long messages and any language, the parts counted as you type), delivery reports (Sent, Delivered), and a notice for each new message, also on the lock screen with the sender only (an administrator can allow the text). Messages are kept in your account's folder, encrypted when "Encrypt my data" is on, and taken off the modem.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the taskbar's network icon shows mobile data's signal as bars, with the operator and the network type (5G, LTE, 3G), on both desktops; the network menu lists mobile data in use or kept in reserve. Settings › Mobile network shows the signal's details (RSRP, RSRQ, SINR, in words too) for placing the computer or an antenna. System health notes modem events (the SIM taken out, the PIN blocked, no network, the module restarting), and the self-test's modem line checks the driver, the SIM, the network and the data connection.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: Settings › Mobile network shows the mobile data used this month on each SIM (counted on this computer, kept across restarts), from the day of the month you choose, with a monthly limit: a notice at 80 % and, if you choose, mobile data turned off at 100 % until the next month (Connect goes on anyway). Mobile data is metered by itself: updates are never downloaded by themselves on it, and Settings offers them with their size ("Download over mobile data: up to 42 MB").

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: mobile data through a cellular modem: Connect and Disconnect in Settings › Mobile network and in quick settings (📶 Mobile data), connected by itself on the SIM's home network (abroad only when roaming is allowed). A cable comes first, then Wi-Fi, then mobile data: it stays connected but unused while Wi-Fi works and carries the traffic within seconds when Wi-Fi drops, with a notice, and Wi-Fi takes over again when it is back. The firewall covers the cellular connection as every other and never treats it as the local network. IPv6-only networks (T-Mobile's) reach IPv4 sites through a CLAT (464XLAT).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: Settings › Mobile network, for a cellular modem's SIM card: unlock it with its PIN (an administrator's password; the tries left are shown), or with its PUK and a new PIN after three wrong PINs (with the warning that ten wrong PUKs block the SIM for good); the operator's settings (APN) found by themselves from the SIM, with Rudolf's own corrections for operators that need the APN's capitals exactly (US Mobile's "PWG"), or typed in exactly as given; mobile data when roaming off unless turned on; the network type (5G, 4G, 3G) where the modem lets it be chosen. Quick settings has Airplane mode: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and the cellular modem off together, and back as they were.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Cellular modems (docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 1): Settings › Network › Cellular modems offers "Turn on this laptop's cellular module" for laptop modules whose radio starts locked (the FCC lock: Lenovo's and Dell's Fibocom, Quectel and Sierra cards), saying what it does; an administrator's name and password turn it on, and it is kept. Modules that Linux supports only partly (Intel's XMM7360 in some ThinkPads) are named there with what is known about them, instead of failing silently. ModemManager comes with QMI, MBIM, QRTR and AT support and the tools its unlock scripts need. Fixed: the modem service started ModemManager again for each of a modem's ports and never stopped it when the modem was unplugged.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: The native desktop's dialogs (Open and Save, Print, Allow access?, Close anyway?, a game's download) now appear over the whole desktop, dimmed and centred, as in the standard desktop, instead of inside the app's window where their buttons could be cut off.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed on the native desktop: a video in full screen showed a black screen; Task Manager listed only its own window (it now lists every window, with Switch to and End task).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: The native desktop's apps now draw sliders, colour boxes, time and date fields, radio buttons and progress bars as the standard desktop does, show the chevron on every drop-down list and 12-hour times with AM and PM.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: The native desktop shows Glacier Lake's northern lights and Spirit Falls' statue, petals and sky lanterns, as the standard desktop does.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed on the native desktop: right-click menus inside apps were cut off at the window's edge (File Explorer's last rows could not be reached); Settings › System health › Log video problems lost its lines whenever another app window opened; apps showed no scrollbars, so text wrapped differently; plain text boxes, and title bars in dark mode, looked different.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed on the native desktop: File Explorer's "Folders on this device" (import and export a folder) was missing and storage showed 0 B; Settings › About showed "Apple GPU" as the graphics; a window's own icon (Flash Player's) was replaced by its app's.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: rudolf-fetch in the Terminal: Rudolf's logo (the nose in red) with this computer's details beside it: Rudolf OS's version, the kernel, the desktop engine, the update channel, the processor, memory, disk and uptime.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: Get in App Store › Rudolf OS Library failed for an app the Library had just updated (Ember Reach 0.4.0): the computer's list still named the older version, so the download was refused as not matching. Rudolf OS now checks the list again and gets the new version.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: beta versions are opt-in: Settings › Update and recovery › Get beta versions (an administrator's name and password to turn on). Turned off, the next update brings the latest stable release, even from a newer beta.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: The native desktop shows the Phone screen and Blitzen exactly as the standard desktop does: apps' text, drop-down lists and check boxes in its windows are drawn as in the standard desktop.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: when memory ran out, the memory guard could close the desktop's own page (it then stopped responding and the browser was restarted, back to the sign-in screen). The desktop now says which page process is its own until that works, the guard checks that it is still that process, and while it is not known no page of the desktop's browser is closed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: printers plugged in by USB: the print dialog lists them as "USB: name" and Settings › Devices shows each one and its kind. Printers that print over USB with IPP (most sold since about 2015) and PostScript printers need the new USB printers system extension; printers that read PDF print straight away; others are named as needing a driver Rudolf OS does not have.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: signed system extensions (Settings › Update and recovery › System extensions): parts such as printer support added to Rudolf OS without a new release, laid over the system read-only at each start and never changing it; only Rudolf OS's own signed ones, installed by an administrator, left out if one would replace a part of Rudolf OS or keeps it from starting, with Start once without extensions.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: The native desktop is the desktop a new installation starts with (it uses less memory and starts faster); a computer that is updated keeps its desktop engine, and Settings offers the native desktop once. Settings › System health › Desktop engine still has Standard and Lite, and Standard is used if Native does not start.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: The native desktop has the screen saver and its lock, as the standard desktop (not while sound plays, a call or a full-screen app is on, or an app keeps the screen on).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: The native desktop has the window keys now, as the standard desktop: Alt+Tab's switcher, Super+Tab's overview of all windows, Super+D, Super+Up and Down, Alt+F4, Super+E, R, I and L, Ctrl+Esc and Super for the start menu, F1, and your own keys from Settings › Keyboard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Linux apps can keep the screen on or the computer awake: a game, a video or a download in a Linux app now holds off the screen saver, the lock, the screen turning off and sleep while it asks.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Devices are now set up by udev, as on other Linux distributions, so Linux apps, Steam and the modem service find hardware the usual way; mdev stays as a fallback if udev cannot start.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: The keyring's own questions are now asked by Rudolf OS: when an app creates a new keyring or needs one unlocked, the desktop asks for its password in Rudolf's own prompt, naming the app, instead of the request failing.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Settings › Privacy › Saved passwords for apps: see which apps keep sign-ins in this account's keyring and remove them; Flatpak apps can now keep theirs too (the Secret portal).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: App Store › Rudolf OS Library says when its list of apps was last checked (and when the Library published it), with a Refresh button at the end of its first line: the list was kept until it stopped working, so a working list days old never showed new apps or updates (Ember Reach on the Vivobook, 2026-11-14)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: A keyring for Linux apps: apps such as the Claude app, VS Code and other Electron apps now keep their sign-ins in the account's own keyring (the Secret Service), unlocked by signing in, instead of warning that GNOME Keyring is not set up or asking again after every restart.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Settings › System health › Log video problems works on the native desktop too (its video and sound warnings, and Oracle's video and sound messages there), and the native desktop's log is now kept across a restart and included in the system report.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Planned: what 1.5.9 had left, moved here on 2026-11-15 (docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 15): the native desktop's comparison with Standard, the official recovery's repair at each start, the Vivobook's call and feature checks, QEMU security checks, Lite's tab fixes, the hotspot, ARM64's test channel, Waydroid and the first phone.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Planned: a keyring for Linux apps (the Secret Service), unlocked by the account's sign-in, so apps such as the Claude app keep their sign-ins without a plain file or a second password.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 4): workspaces as on Standard: the taskbar's 1 2 3 buttons, Ctrl+Alt+Left and Right (with Shift the window goes too), a window's Move to workspace N, the taskbar listing the shown workspace's windows, "Workspace N" said in a toast (compared with Chromium: new same_t.sh cases ws2, ws2-dark, ws2-left; the same steps on both engines: new test iso/qt/native/wsbeh_t.js). Fixed: a notification with no text under its title is as tall as the page's.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 3's last part): the taskbar at the left or the right of the screen, as on Standard: a column as wide as its widest part, the start button, the pinned apps, the open windows one under the other and the tray at the bottom; the desktop's icons, windows, the start menu and the pop-ups placed beside it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Changed: the plan: signed system extensions (Part 13): drivers, firmware and tools added to one computer as signed read-only layers over the unchanged base, instead of a conventional package manager; USB printers (Part 8) are their first use.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 3's last part, first half): the network's pop-up (the adapters, the one in use, Network Settings…); a notification shows in the screen's corner as on Standard (sliding in, gone after its time, a click doing its own action or opening the notifications' centre, ⚡ Why?), not inside the window of the app that sent it, and is in the centre and counted on the bell at once; the taskbar's 🎙️ while an app uses the microphone, muting it for everything with a click (🔇); the bell shows 🔕 with Do not disturb and counts the notifications come since signing in; Meta+N and Meta+A; a setting changed in one app's window reaches the others. Fixed: a dismissed notification could come back for a moment; the shell's dark pop-ups and menus followed the dark theme's switch alone, not the light or dark mode; Settings asked for at a page by another app's window opens at that page.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 3): quick settings (☰: its switches, the network, Lock, Settings, Power) and the notifications' centre (🔔: Do not disturb, Clear all, each notification with its time, ✕ and Blitzen's Why? for a failure), drawn as the desktop page draws them on Standard; the battery's button opens Settings' System health.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 3, second part): the calendar under the taskbar's clock (the month's weeks, today, the Calendar's events and the next four, the months before and after, Open Calendar, a day double-clicked opening the Calendar there) and the volume's pop-up (its slider, Mute, Desktop sounds…), drawn as the desktop page draws them on Standard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 3, first part): the taskbar's right-click menus as the page's, row by row: the taskbar's own (Show desktop, Restore all windows, Cascade windows, Close all windows, Taskbar settings), the start button's, a pinned app's (with each app's own rows: Oracle's New private tab), a window's button's (read from the window's page: Restore, Minimize, Maximize, Always on top, Center on screen, Pin or Unpin, Print / Save as PDF…, Close, Force quit), the sound's, the network's and the clock's (compared with Chromium: new same_t.sh cases tbm-*; the same steps on both engines: new test iso/qt/native/tbbeh_t.js). Fixed: the shell's menus are placed as the page's (above the pointer when they would not fit below); Open Command Prompt opens the page's Command Prompt (terminal).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 2): the desktop's widgets (the clock, the calendar, the sticky note, the system monitor and the weather) drawn by the shell exactly as the page draws them (compared with Chromium: new same_t.sh cases widgets, widgets-ask, widgets-top, widgets-over, widget-picker), each where the account left it: dragged by its header, removed with its ✕, added from the desktop's menu (Add a widget…, the page's picker), the note typed in as the page's textarea (its keys, menu, undo and copy and paste), the weather from Open-Meteo (a click opens Weather), each with the page's timers; saved as the page saves them (bd95widgets, kept by rudolfd until an app's page takes it). The same steps on both engines: new test iso/qt/native/wgbeh_t.js. App windows' pages no longer run the widgets' timers.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 1, second part, drag and drop): a desktop icon follows the pointer as it is dragged; a file dropped on an app's window opens in that app in a window of its own (as the page's __dropFileOnWindow), a file or a shortcut of your own dropped on the Trash goes there; an Explorer window's files dragged onto another window (another page) are dropped there as on Standard (moved between Explorer windows, opened in an app's window). Fixed: on Native each window's page now sees the files the other windows changed (a page that saved tells the others, which read them again), so a window no longer shows or saves back old files. Fixed: an app's window on Native showed its page at the size GTK first asked for (larger than the window, its right and bottom cut off) and was not drawn again where another window uncovered it (the shell's window manager replaced GDK's own X events for its windows); the shell no longer crashes when a window closes while its frame is still there; chosen desktop icons stay chosen when the desktop's list comes again.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 1, second part): the Desktop folder's files and folders as icons in the page's places; the page's right-click menus (the desktop's, a file's, the Trash's, an app's) and its Rename and Open with dialogs drawn by the shell as the page draws them (compared with Chromium: new same_t.sh cases desk-files, desk-menu, file-menu, file-rename, file-openwith); New folder, New text document, Rename (F2), Move to Trash (Delete), Open with, Properties and Empty trash done by the page itself in a hidden one-app window (#app=do-desk, #app=do-fs). Fixed: an app's window or a hidden page no longer squeezes the desktop's icon places into its own size (its grid is the screen's).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: the native desktop (Native engine) now looks as Standard does, measured part by part against the desktop page in Chromium (new test iso/qt/native/same_t.sh, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, "The rule"): the taskbar in its five styles, its buttons' styles and the accent colour's modes (the page's sizes, font, corners, gloss, edges and shadow; the network, sound and battery as the page draws them; the workspaces' buttons; the notifications' count), the desktop's icons (the page's font, wrapping, picture and text shadows), the start menu (the page's own list, with its search box, headings and greyed rows), the windows' frames and title bars in their five styles and colour modes (the page's sizes, round corners, shadow and resize handles; an app's window opens at the page's size and place), and the sign-in and lock screens. Meta+L locks the screen; Start › Shut Down... shows the page's Power dialog.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: Fixed: with Oracle's Dark pages on, part of a video could be drawn as a negative: on YouTube, while the mouse was on the progress bar, the video from the player's left edge to the pointer. A layer over a video (a picture, a canvas, or anything with its own background picture, with a blur behind it) inverted the video under it once more, and so did a video inside such a layer; each is now turned back only once. Also fixed: a dark page whose colour is set on the page itself rather than on its body was turned light.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (2026-11-20, release 2026112014)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 1, first part): the desktop's icons, as the page shows them for the account (its shortcuts, pictures and places), on the page's grid at the icon size and display scaling: a double-click opens, dragging moves an icon to the nearest free place (kept by rudolfd), Arrange icons by name, Refresh, and the icon's and the desktop's menus. Files on the desktop come next.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Summary: A native desktop to try (Native, test), Browse with Tor in Oracle, protections against a directed attack, developer mode with custom builds and an official recovery, more memory for games, calls and microphone tests, and Save and Open dialogs with document tabs (docs/plan-1.5.9.md)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: Browse with Tor on Standard: clicking the Tor window's bookmarks bar, address box or buttons no longer jumps back to the desktop, and the Tor window is signed in as the desktop is instead of showing the sign-in screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the self-test run over the read-only development link failed its listeners check when a Linux app was open (it cannot look into other users' programs there); it now says so instead.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Browse with Tor in Oracle: an onion button at the right end of the bookmarks bar sends that window's tabs through Tor, in a private Tor window of its own (Rudolf's Chromium through Tor: sites do not see the computer's address, and no site's name or WebRTC address leaves outside Tor); pressing it again brings the tabs back to a normal window. The window says plainly that this is not Tor Browser's anonymity and links Tor Browser (plan 16.2).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: WordPro's hyperlinks as in other word processors: link to a web address, a place in the document (a heading or a bookmark), a file on this computer or an e-mail address with a subject; the text to show and a ScreenTip; bookmarks; a link's right-click menu (Open, Edit, Copy address, Remove); typed web and e-mail addresses becoming links; and a list of every link with Go to, Edit, Remove and Remove all.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Tor in the system (for Oracle's Browse with Tor, plan 16.1): it runs only while a Tor window is open, as a user of its own, listening only on this computer (127.0.0.1:9050), with nothing kept on the disk; System health notes when it starts, is ready, stops or fails.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the Save As box of Notepad, WordLite, WordPro and Paint (and the Run box) ignored typing: its Enter handler cancelled every other key.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Notepad, WordLite and WordPro save and open through a dialog like the File Explorer: folders, a name, and the file type from a list (Notepad: text, Markdown, web page, Lua, CSV, JSON, batch; WordLite and WordPro: rich document, web page, text). Notepad and WordLite keep several documents in tabs under their buttons (New, Open, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Tab), a file opened from elsewhere joins the open window as a tab, and unsaved tabs are asked about.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: another Rudolf OS stick plugged in (an older one, for example) never showed in the File Explorer: every disk with a Rudolf OS partition was hidden, not only the one Rudolf OS runs from. It now shows; its data partition opens read-only and its start-up parts stay hidden.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Settings › Volume Controls › Microphones has a list of the microphones (the one chosen becomes every app's, a call's too) and a Test button: an equalizer and a level meter show what the chosen microphone hears.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: Oracle on Native (test): a link opened in a new window, Ctrl+N or a web page's file from another app opens an Oracle window of its own, as on Standard, not a window inside Oracle's; closing Oracle while a download is arriving no longer shows Chromium's "Download is in progress" question: the window goes, the download is still put in Downloads and told, then Chromium closes; files saved in Oracle and in an app window that is open are seen by each other at once (before, one could overwrite the other); text copied in Oracle stays on the clipboard after Oracle closes; the volume keys' indicator appears at the top of the screen, not inside a window.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: calls heard nothing on laptops whose built-in microphones are on another sound chip than the speakers (the Vivobook's AMD microphones): the headset jack's microphone was made the default even with nothing plugged in. It is now the default only when a headset is plugged in.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Oracle's bookmarks bar ends with a "+" that adds a bookmark by its address, from the browsing history (newest first, searchable), or as a file on this computer (a document or a PDF).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: choosing a file in the desktop's own file picker (Open a presentation or a spreadsheet, and others) answered as if nothing had been chosen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: the plan: Browse with Tor in Oracle (Part 16): a button on the bookmarks bar sends that window through Tor, which runs only while it is used.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: a USB tethering link or cable without internet took over from a working Wi-Fi, cutting the computer off (found with a MiFi without a data plan on the same network range as the home router). A new wired connection is now used only once the internet answers through it, and is tried again every 30 seconds; until then the Wi-Fi keeps the route and its DNS, and the network menu and Settings say "No internet" for it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Recovery mode in the boot menu now starts its own start-up file, recovery.efi, signed with the Rudolf OS key. It starts only the official recovery system kept on this computer (system/r), after checking that its release list is signed by the official key (never by Developer mode's extra key) and that every file has the size and SHA-256 that list says. A changed or wrongly signed recovery system is refused, with the file and the reason shown, and nothing else is started in its place.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the self-test's listeners check failed while a Linux app ran (the Claude app's own sockets inside Debian, Chromium's newer socket folder), and its Debian check failed when run over the read-only development link; a Linux app's own sockets inside its container are now said as such, and the Debian check says when it cannot look.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: the self-test says which system runs (the Official Rudolf OS, or a Custom build in Developer mode with the key that signed it), and every development link result names the system that answered.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the development link could not be switched on with the official builds. It needed Developer mode, which can only be turned on by trusting a developer's key. It now has its own switch, "Allow the development link on this computer" (an administrator's password; unticking it ends the link), and Developer mode moved from Update and recovery to Settings › Security, just above the development link.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed (security): the display needs authorization. X no longer lets every program on the computer watch the screen, read the keys and type into the desktop: it starts with a new cookie only root can read, and only root, the desktop's user and the signed-in account's own Linux user may use it (taken back at sign-out). Debian's Linux programs and Wine now run as the signed-in account's own Linux user too, with the account's folder as their home (Wine's programs and their Start menu entries are the account's), and Library packages started from the desktop as well; another account's programs cannot reach them (plan 15.3, second step).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed (security): each account is its own Linux user (uid 1001 and up), made and removed with the account. Its files belong to it alone, and the Linux apps and Flatpak apps it starts run as it, with its own session bus and desktop portal, so one account's apps cannot read another's files; signing out stops all of them. Existing accounts' files are given to their users at the first start (ownership only, logged; what cannot be moved is named in System health). The desktop's page and API now also check the desktop's own user. Debian and Wine follow in the next step.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New (security): the development link can only look at the computer (read files and logs, take screenshots) unless "Allow changes to this computer" is ticked in Settings › Security › Development link, which needs an administrator's password and is unticked again at every start. Read-only is enforced by the system: its commands run as an unprivileged user in a read-only view of the files, without the link's token; bringing files and restarting are refused. The banner says which.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed (security): fewer and harder doors. A list of everything that listens on the computer (TCP ports and Unix sockets), with who may use each and how it checks; the self-test fails when something listens that the list does not name. The system programs are built with the stack protector, FORTIFY_SOURCE=3, PIE, full RELRO and control-flow protection, and each release checks the flags on the built programs. rudolfd's request parsing and JSON are fuzzed before each release; the fuzzing found and fixed a read past the end of a JSON string ending in a broken escape, and a request with a negative or second Content-Length is now refused.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New (security): a daily check compares the Chromium and the kernel of the latest release with the newest ones Ubuntu has published (the chromium snap, Ubuntu's mainline builds of the release's kernel series) and opens one issue "Security update available: …" when either is newer, never a second while one is open; it builds and releases nothing (it replaces the Chromium check). Settings › About shows the release's Chromium and its date.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed (security): the development link is off unless it is being used. It can be switched on only in Developer mode, by an administrator whose password rudolfd now checks itself; Ask first is on again after every restart; the link is off after a restart unless "Keep on after restarting" is ticked (off by default), and turns itself off after 4 hours without a command, with a notification. System health shows whether it is on, since when, who switched it on and its last command.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed (security): WordPro's cleaning of documents and pasted text could be got round (a slash for a space before onerror, an SVG animation, javascript: links), so a crafted document could run script in the desktop. It now uses the browser's own parser (safeHtml) and removes everything that can run. A test opens 19 hostile files in every app; a new check (htmlsinks, run with deadcheck) catches new places that make HTML from data; and the page now forbids plug-in content and outside <base> addresses.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed (security): rudolfd gave the desktop's page, with its API token and the page's stored data, to any program on the computer, so a Linux app, a Wine program or a Flatpak could use the system API, which runs as root. Now the page and the API answer only the desktop's own processes (its memory group) and root; others are refused and System health says so (Security). The kernel also gets Yama, so programs cannot read the browser's memory either. The self-test checks both.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: the plan: on the native desktop, Oracle will run on Chromium with Rudolf's tab shell, as on Standard (real tabs, the same sign-ins and private tabs), started only while Oracle is open (plan Part 12, step 8).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Display Properties says "Note: Dynamic effects are disabled on power-saver mode." under Dynamic Backgrounds, only while power saver (or battery saver) is on, when Spirit Falls' petals and lanterns and Glacier Lake's aurora stand still.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: Rudolf OS's calendars show weeks from Sunday to Saturday (they began on Monday): the Calendar app, the calendar under the taskbar's clock and the calendar widget.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: private browsing in Oracle: New private tab in Oracle's ☰ menu, Ctrl+Shift+N, and when you right-click Oracle's icon (on the taskbar, in the Start menu, on the desktop, or an open Oracle window's taskbar button). A private window is marked 🕶️ Private in dark violet; its pages are not kept in History, its cookies and site data are kept in memory only (with Standard and Lite) and forgotten when the last private window closes; pop-ups from it stay private. Help › Privacy explains what is kept (bookmarks, downloads) and who can still see what you visit.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: the plans: on the native desktop Rudolf OS must appear and work exactly as it does on Standard (Chromium): every part of the native shell, and later every native app, is compared with Standard's in screenshots and behaviour, and each difference is a bug (plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, plan-2.0.md).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: Native (test)'s six bugs seen on the Vivobook (plan 12.3b step 7): a picture of your own shows from the first start (rudolfd makes the shell's copy from the page's database mirror when no page has given it yet); the screen shows the arrow, not X's bare cross; the taskbar follows Display Properties' display scaling and draws the apps' pictures as the page does (not emoji), with the version on the start button; drop-downs in app windows are drawn as in Lite (the page now knows Native's app windows are WebKit); the development link's red banner is drawn once by the shell at the top of the screen (windows kept below it, End now, and it asks about commands itself), no longer inside every app window, where it hid Settings' search box.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: the plans: Rudolf OS goes native (decided from the native engine's measurements on the Vivobook: 854 MB used at idle against Standard's 1,110 MB). Native (test)'s bugs seen on the Vivobook are fixed in 1.5.9 (plan Part 12, step 7); the native shell gets everything the web desktop's shell has and becomes the default in 1.6.0 (plan-1.6.0.md Part 12); the apps are rewritten natively, one by one, for 2.0 (docs/plan-2.0.md).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Settings › System health › Desktop engine › Native (test): the native desktop engine's prototype (plan Part 12), with Lite's safeguards: on trial until its sign-in screen appears, and given up for Standard (said in System health and Settings) after a start that does not get there; never in Recovery mode. Ctrl+Alt+Backspace turns it off too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: the native desktop engine's prototype is a window manager too (plan Part 12): every window gets a title bar in the title bar styles and colours, with minimise, maximise and close, moving and resizing, focus on click, full screen for games and videos, dialogs centred over their window, and the open windows on the taskbar.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: rudolf-native, the native desktop engine's prototype (plan Part 12): the wallpaper, the taskbar in its styles and accent colours, the pinned apps, the tray, the clock, the start menu and the sign-in and lock screens drawn natively (GTK), each app in a WebKit window of its own, all sharing one WebKit process. Not offered in Settings yet.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: rudolfd answers the native desktop engine's questions (plan Part 12): the accounts for its sign-in screen (never a hash), the sign-in itself, checked as the desktop page checks it and opening the account's encrypted folder, and the desktop's settings, pinned apps and start menu; the desktop page gives it the start menu's list and a copy of your own background picture. Written down in docs/api.md.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: the desktop page's one-app mode (for the native desktop engine being prototyped, plan Part 12): index.html#app=NAME starts one app alone, filling the window, signed in from the native session; closing the app writes its files and closes the page.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Display Properties › Taskbar › Buttons: the taskbar's buttons (start, pinned apps, open windows, workspaces, the tray) in a style of their own (Standard, Wireframe, Monochrome, Candy, Retro), in the accent colour as Normal, Negative or Complementary when "Match the theme colours" is ticked, otherwise in each style's own colours.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: plugging in an Android phone with USB debugging or file transfer on no longer says Rudolf OS has no driver for it: apps use those directly, without a driver.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: the PDF Viewer prints (🖨️ Print, or Ctrl+P): the PDF itself, on its own paper size, to a network printer (IPP Everywhere / AirPrint) or saved as a copy, through the same print dialog as WordPro.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the self-test said the desktop's browser was not in the desktop's memory group when it was.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the start-up chime plays when the sign-in screen appears, not only after the first key or click there (on installed Rudolf OS; the browser version still needs a key or click first, as browsers require).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the sign-in page after a start-up showed a teal background instead of the desktop's picture: it now remembers which background the desktop has (your picture, a drawn background, or the colours) rather than how it looked at that moment, and a drawn background shows its light or dark picture for the time of day.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Settings › Date, time and language › Share my language with apps (on by default): Library apps such as games are told Rudolf OS's language, when they start and whenever it changes, so they can show their own menus in it. Off, apps are not told which language you use.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the screen saver no longer stays off for good after something went full screen in a window that was then minimised or hidden (that also kept game mode on), or after a saver's picture was taken away; why the saver waits (something full screen, sound playing, a microphone in use) is written to the page log.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: the Feather Sky static background: Rudolf's logo in a sky of swirling white feathers (a night-blue version in dark mode).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: two static backgrounds: Carbon Fibre (Rudolf's logo in brushed metal on carbon fibre, for work and gaming) and Moonlit Stag (Rudolf on a boulder above a mountain lake, at night in dark mode and at dawn in light mode).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: Display Properties no longer has the colour presets (Sunset, Ocean, Classic Teal and the others, there since 1.1); Background style and Color 1 / Color 2 still make simple colour and pattern backgrounds. The drawn backgrounds are now in two rows: Dynamic Backgrounds, the ones that move (Spirit Falls, Glacier Lake), and Static Backgrounds (Alpine Peak, Obsidian Waves, Gilded Crest, Teal Prism, Slate Panels). Both still have a light and a dark version.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Display Properties › Title bars: the windows' title bars in the taskbar's styles (Standard, Wireframe, Monochrome, Candy, Retro), in the accent colour as Normal, Negative or Complementary. The window you are using has the colour; the others stay grey.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Search in Settings: a search box at the top of Settings. As you type, a drop-down lists the pages, sections and settings that still match, each with where it is underneath in smaller text (Settings › Network Settings › Wi-Fi). Choose one (click, or the arrow keys and Enter) to open its page with that setting highlighted.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: game mode puts Oracle's background tabs to sleep to free memory for the game. A sleeping tab keeps its address and shows 💤; selecting it loads it again. Tabs playing sound or holding typed text stay awake. Blitzen's model is unloaded too (unless Blitzen is in front), and system, Linux app and Debian updates wait until the game ends. Settings › System health › Memory can turn it off.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: when memory is getting low, Rudolf OS warns before it has to close a page, also inside a full-screen game ("Memory is almost full: save your progress if you can"), and game mode puts more tabs to sleep.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: the desktop page is about 2 MB smaller (5.5 to 3.5 MB): the dynamic backgrounds' pictures, the fonts and the Super Nintendo player are now separate files, and SpreadsheetPro and PresentPro load the first time they are opened.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: with compressed memory on, idle memory is moved into it sooner (swappiness 180), so a game that suddenly needs more finds room; the memory warning now comes whenever free memory is low.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: the graphics driver keeps at most 64 MB of spare memory for reuse (it could grow to half the memory over a long session).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Task Manager › Performance shows where the memory goes: programs and pages, the file cache, the kernel, graphics, the SSD's buffer, compressed memory, and what Linux cannot itemise while the system is protected.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Task Manager › Performance has Clear cache, which frees the memory holding recently used files at once; game mode does the same when a game starts, so the game finds free memory as it loads.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: when a game starts, apps running in the background with no window (such as Discord) are offered to be quit, in a notice inside the game with a button; nothing is quit unless you press it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: Wi-Fi dropped for about 45 seconds when it tried a radio of the router that never answers (the Vivobook's router's 2.4 GHz radio). Such a radio is now left out reliably, and remembered for a day, restarts included.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Settings › Network › Wi-Fi › Radios of this network: each radio of the router (2.4, 5 and 6 GHz under one name) with its channel, signal and state, and a switch to stop this computer using one; it also says which bands this computer's Wi-Fi has.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: "Why does the Wi-Fi drop?" (Settings › Network › Wi-Fi, or asking Blitzen about a Wi-Fi problem): Blitzen reads the Wi-Fi's log, the kernel's Wi-Fi messages and the radios, and recommends only the Wi-Fi settings that exist.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Improved: Blitzen's Wi-Fi answer now rests on findings worked out from the logs (which radio did not answer, how strong each radio is) and names the setting to change, instead of retelling earlier versions from the documentation.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the Wi-Fi tool that reads the Wi-Fi chip's bands (iw) is now in the system, so "This computer's Wi-Fi radios" and the radios' bands show on real computers (without it the list was empty).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: "This computer's Wi-Fi radios" (Settings › Network › Wi-Fi), a drop-down menu with a check by each of the computer's own Wi-Fi radios (2.4 / 5 / 6 GHz) that is on. Only an administrator can change it, with their password, and Rudolf OS never changes it by itself.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Security: Library web apps run in a sandbox of their own (no access to the desktop, its storage or rudolfd), talking to it only through the game kit's messages; an app from an outside developer gets only what it asks for and you allow when you first open it (saves, game controllers, full screen). Needed before apps from outside developers can be in the Library.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: an official recovery system on every installed computer: the newest official release that started successfully is kept (without using extra room), and Recovery mode starts it. Only releases signed with the official key ever become the recovery system.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Developer mode (Settings › Update and recovery, administrators): install your own Rudolf OS builds, signed with your publisher key, from your own address, after a strong warning, a typed confirmation and the password. Settings › About says whether the running system is the Official Rudolf OS or a Custom build, and with which key.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Return to official Rudolf OS (Settings › Update and recovery, and offered in Recovery mode): Developer mode off, the official Rudolf OS at the next restart, keeping your accounts, files and apps or erasing everything; the custom build is removed once the official one has started.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: User Settings › Developer: make a publisher key for your own games and builds. Its private half is kept only in a backup file protected by a passphrase; the account keeps the public half and its fingerprint.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: docs/custom-builds.md, how to make your own Rudolf OS (keys, update address, Library) and go back to the official one; its commands are checked in CI.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: packages from outside developers, through a chain of trust: the Rudolf OS Library certifies a developer (their key and the names they may use); their apps install only as desktop apps in the sandbox, under those names; the Library can revoke a developer or a package, which is then disabled on every computer at its next check.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: video calls: with the Lite engine, Google Meet, Zoom's web client, Teams and other call sites open in Chromium's window (Ubuntu's WebKitGTK has no WebRTC); test calls on both engines in CI.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: "In a call" in the taskbar (🎙️ while an app uses the microphone; one click mutes it for everything); a call keeps the screen saver, the lock and sleep away; changing the sound output moves the call too, and a headset plugged in takes over.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: cellular modems are recognised (ModemManager, started only while a modem is plugged in): Settings › Network shows each one with its SIM, operator and signal. Connecting with a SIM comes in 1.6.0.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Share this connection (Settings › Network, administrators): the computer's Wi-Fi becomes a hotspot (WPA2/WPA3) for other devices, sharing a cable, a phone's USB tethering or a modem (or the Wi-Fi itself on chips that can do both). Off by default and after a restart.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Settings › Apps › Calls to phones: what Google Voice, Zoom Phone and Teams Phone need to call phone numbers; a phone number clicked on a web page asks how to call it (Google Voice, Teams, the phone on the desk, or copy it), once if you like.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: Chromium comes only from Ubuntu's open-source Chromium (the snap). When it cannot be fetched, the release keeps the Chromium it has, instead of taking another kind of browser; it never goes back to an older version.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: when a system file does not match its release, the start-up and Task Manager say so plainly, with its size, instead of a low-level error.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: on the Native desktop (test), Oracle runs in Rudolf OS's own Chromium with real browser tabs, as on Standard: websites open as real pages, sign-ins are kept in the same place as on Standard, and one Chromium serves every Oracle window, started with the first and closed with the last. Its windows are framed by the native desktop like every other app; without Chromium, Oracle opens as before and says so once (plan 12.3c).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: on the Native desktop (test), an app opened from Oracle (a downloaded file, a link to another app) opens in a window of its own, as from any other app (plan 12.3c, step 5).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: on the Native desktop (test), Oracle's notifications show in the screen's corner and in the notifications' centre like every other app's, and clicking one does what it says (plan 12.3c, step 5).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop (test), Ctrl+W in a website in Oracle closed Oracle's whole window, and Ctrl+Q closed every Oracle window. Oracle's keys now work as on Standard: Ctrl+W closes the tab, Ctrl+T opens one, Ctrl+Shift+N opens a private window of its own, and Ctrl+Q and Alt+F4 do what they do on Standard (plan 12.3c, step 5).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop (test), the desktop's own full screen in Oracle's window (a video or a game shown full screen by the desktop) filled only Oracle's window. It now fills the screen, as on Standard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop (test), Open with in Oracle or in another app's window opened the chosen app inside that window. It now opens the file in a window of its own, as on Standard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: on the Native desktop (test), a website's download could be taken by two windows at once, one saying it was saved and the other that it stopped. Oracle files every download, as the desktop does on Standard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.8 (2026-11-12)
docs.t: Summary: Diagnosing a computer that does not start, full rescue sticks, Oracle's tabs in the Lite desktop, mobile data, Android phones and tablets, and new dynamic backgrounds (docs/plan-1.5.8.md)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.8 (2026-11-12)
docs.t: Fixed: when the memory guard ends a web page, the desktop now leaves full screen at once and says so, also when only a frame inside a page was ended (a game on a website), which left the screen full screen on a broken frame before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.8 (2026-11-12)
docs.t: Fixed: a page closed to free memory while full screen (a game in an Oracle tab) left the screen full screen and black, and Ctrl+Alt+Del's Task Manager opened behind it. A tab that ends now leaves full screen, and Task Manager and the shutdown dialog leave full screen first. Settings pages also no longer react to changes on a page shown before them.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.8 (2026-11-12)
docs.t: Fixed: the moving parts of the dynamic backgrounds (northern lights, petals, lanterns) kept running behind games and over a picture of your own, which made Friday Night Funkin' choppy. They now run only when they can be seen, stop in power saver, and use half the frames on battery. Choosing a dynamic background now puts it on the screen even when a picture was set. Fixed: System health showed memory 1,024 times too large ("1201.3 GB of 3415.5 GB"). The battery's time left now follows the power used over the last few minutes, not one moment's reading.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.8 (2026-11-12)
docs.t: New: Make a Rudolf OS USB stick makes a full rescue stick, or none. It checks the stick's size before erasing anything, keeps the system it copies a second time as the stick's rescue system (no extra room; updates on the stick never change it), and starts that rescue system when no updated system on the stick can. A stick that could not be finished is cleared instead of being left half-made. Settings › Storage says what each plugged-in Rudolf OS stick holds, and a boot-files-only image says so in its boot menu.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.8 (2026-11-12)
docs.t: New: games from the Rudolf OS Library, starting with Fault Lines (a logic puzzle: clear the ground without opening a fault; three fields and a Daily one). It is in the Start menu and App Store › Games, and downloads its small package (16 KB) the first time. Best times are kept with your account, and the game pauses when its window is minimised or the computer locks.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.8 (2026-11-12)
docs.t: New: Night Flight, a bullet-hell shooter from the Rudolf OS Library: Rudolf flies up through a winter night firing lasers from his glowing nose, charges a piercing beam, grazes bullets and saves corrupted friends.
